BUDGETARY ALLOCATION AND EXPENDITURE 
Recommendation (Para No.2.6 and 3.10) 
5. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“The Committee note that the actual expenditure of the Ministry of Minority 
Affairs has gone down considerably during previous years. The Ministry could 
spend only ₹837.68 crore and ₹1,032.65 crore out of ₹2,612.66 (RE) crore 
and ₹2,608.93 (RE) crore during the year 2022-23 and 2023-24. The 
situation did not improve in 2024-25 as the Ministry were able to spend only 
₹919.10 crore out of budgetary allocation of ₹3,183.24 crore (BE) by 31 
December, 2024. The Committee have been apprised that the Ministry have 
not been able to spend the budgetary allocation as several Schemes such as 
Free Coaching and Allied Scheme, Nai Udaan, Scheme of Providing Education 
in Madrasas/ Minorities (SPEMM), etc, have been discontinued and PM-VIKAS 
Scheme launched in 2023-24 did not initiate. Further, the amount allocated 
during 2022-23 to 2024-25 under various Scholarship Schemes of the 
Ministry could not be spent because these Schemes are under consideration 
for approval since 2022-23 as they are being harmonised with the Schemes 
of other line Ministries, viz. Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs. The Committee strongly believe that the Ministry of 
Minority Affairs are making all efforts to achieve the mission of the Ministry 
by streamlining and strengthening the prevailing System so that the 
deserving Minorities can avail the benefits of the Schemes and the funds are 
not misused. The Committee feel that the steps taken by the Ministry were 
necessary in order to harmonize the system with the welfare Schemes of 
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and Ministry of Tribal Affairs and 
hope that these steps will improve the implementation of the Schemes and 
enhance the socio-economic condition of six notified minority communities in 
the country. Since the Ministry of Minority Affairs are in process of 
streamlining/strengthening the prevailing System, the Committee expect that 
the necessary approvals will be obtained by the Ministry at the earliest so 
that the allocated Budget of ₹3,350.00 crore for 2025-26 is fruitfully utilised. 
The Committee, therefore, recommend the Ministry of Minority Affairs to 
vigorously pursue with the concerned Ministries/ Departments for the 
pending approvals and keep the administrative machinery of the Ministry 
ready for immediate implementation of the Schemes as soon as they are 
approved.” 


3 
 
6. The Ministry of Minority Affairs, in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted 
as under:- 
 “The Observations of Hon’ble Committee have been noted for compliance.  
Under the Nai Udaan scheme, financial support was provided to candidates 
who qualify in the preliminary examinations conducted by Union Public 
Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), State Public 
Service Commissions (SPSCs). No other Ministry / Department provide such 
support to their beneficiaries. Hence, in order to align with the practices and 
schemes followed by other Ministries and to attain uniformity, it had been 
decided to discontinue this scheme w.e.f. 2022-23. 
Under Free Coaching and Allied Schemes (Naya Savera), coaching were 
provided to students from minority community to empower and prepare 
them for competitive and entrance examinations. The New Education Policy 
2020 does not support coaching programs; thus, the Ministry decide to 
discontinue the scheme w.e.f. 2022-23. 
Scholarship: 
After taking cognizance of media reports in the year 2020 regarding 
siphoning of Scholarship fund, the matter was referred to the Central Bureau 
of Investigation. Also, States were shared suggestive measures to 
incorporate in implementation of Scholarship Schemes. 
In the year 2023, a third party evaluation study, conducted by this Ministry, 
highlighted some irregularities, wherein out of sampled 1,572 institutes, 830 
institutes were found to be either fake/ partially fake or non-operational. 
Observing the seriousness of the issue, Aadhaar based bio-metric 
authentication drive was conducted in which about 27 lakh students and 
verifying officials were to be verified. After the drive, about 18.87 lakh 
students were finally verified for the year 2022-23. Subsequently, in order to 
make the system more robust, Aadhaar Payment Bridge System has been 
introduced for disbursement of scholarships.  
In the year 2024-25, a special drive for verification was held in the North 
Eastern States wherein, fake beneficiaries and verifying authorities were 
recorded. These were for the academic year 2021-22 and 2022-23. This 
exhibited that due diligence was not done by the States in implementing the 
Scholarship Schemes of Minority Affairs in some institutes. States have filed 
FIRs in this regard. Besides, the States have been given additional list of 
suspicious institutes (based on red flags generated by National Informatics 
Centers- National Scholarship Portal) to get them verified/ inspected and 

4 
 
take punitive actions against fraudulent elements. However, reports from the 
states are still awaited.  
In order to prevent duplicity of benefits, MoMA has also asked all the States 
to integrate their State Scholarship Portals with the National Scholarship 
Portal so that de-duplication can be done and one-student one-benefit could 
be ensured. However, the efforts by the States are yet to take a logical 
shape. In such circumstances, approval of Schemes could not be accorded 
by the competent authority and thus, the Ministry could not spend allocated 
funds under the three Scholarship Schemes. This Ministry endeavors to 
implement these schemes at the earliest.”

6 
 
for the allocated Budget from the action taken reply of the Ministry. The

find that problem still persists and the Ministry have not been able to

CHAPTER-II 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE GOVERNMENT 
Recommendation (Para No. 4.8) 
The Committee note that the Ministry of Minority Affairs is implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Virasaat Ka Samvardhan since 2023-24 by converging five erstwhile 
Schemes namely Seekho Aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and 
Nai Manzil. The Committee find that the Ministry spent ₹83.51 crore out of Revised 
Estimate of ₹169.00 crore in 2022-23. After the convergence of independent 
Schemes in PM-VIKAS, the Ministry could spend only 209.42 crore out of RE of 
₹325.86 crore during 2023-24 and ₹124.08 crore out of ₹230.00 crore upto 31 
December, 2024 during 2024-25 to meet the committed liability of 2023-24 and 
2024-25 relating to the erstwhile Schemes. The PM-VIKAS Scheme, however, could 
not be implemented during these years as the guidelines of the Schemes could not 
be approved. The Committee feel that the Ministry should have timely initiated the 
proposal for approval of guidelines to avoid the extraordinary delay. The Committee 
now expect that the guidelines have since been approved, the targeted 
beneficiaries will not have to wait anymore to avail the benefit of the Scheme. The 
Committee hope that the approval of the proposal to integrate the portal of the 
Ministry with National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) etc. will not be delayed 
and the tie up proposed under the Scheme with National Institute of Design (NID), 
National Institute of Fashion Technology and Expert Promotion Council for 
Handicrafts will be finalized and executed at the earliest. The Committee would like 
the Ministry to sanction the proposals received for approval without any delay and 
take necessary action to ensure that the proposals are approved in a time bound 
manner. The Committee may like to be intimated of the action taken in this regard.        
 
Reply of the Government 
The observation of the Hon’ble Committee has been noted for compliance. 
Since the approval of the PM VIKAS guidelines, the Ministry has signed 
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with its knowledge partners including 
National Institute of Design (NID), National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), 
National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) and Export Promotion Council for 
Handicrafts (EPCH) under the scheme. 
The Ministry has held Screening and Empowered committee meetings with 
various stakeholders under the PM VIKAS scheme to deliberate and approve the 

8 
 
proposals received for implementation of the scheme by two (02) institutions 
namely Delhi Sikh Gurudwara Management Committee (DSGMC) and State Institute 
of Hotel Management (SIHM), Manipur for 31,600 and 7,950 beneficiaries 
respectively. 
The Ministry has also signed an MOU with DSGMC and allocated the project 
of 31,600 candidates under PM VIKAS Scheme. 
Ministry of Minority Affairs  OM No. G-20014/02/2025- Budget  Dated   
19.06.2025

covered under PMJVK were increased from 90 Districts to 308 Districts in 33

Ministry should make an action plan to utilize the allocated funds so that they may 
not be reduced at the RE stage. The Committee would like to recommend the 
Ministry to popularize the Scheme so that the proposals are received from 
concerned Organisations and State Governments and take necessary measures to 
approve the proposals received in a time bound manner. They would also like to 
suggest the Ministry to provide the technical and administrative support to the 
implementing Agencies so that they are able to send complete proposals and the 
unnecessary delay due to the receipt of incomplete proposals is avoided. 
 
Reply of the Government 
The observation of the Hon’ble Committee has been noted for compliance. 
It may be informed that the Ministry of Minority Affairs is putting all efforts 
to make the States/Union Territories compliant to the PFMS and SNA Guidelines, 
reduction in the unspent balances available in the States/UTs treasuries and the 

9 
 
completion of old approved projects. Regular Regional Review Meetings/ re-
conciliation are being done to pursue the States/UTs for speedy completion of the 
approved project units and to release the funds to compliant States/UTs.  
The BE for 2025-26 in respect of PMJVK Scheme has been increased from 
₹910.90 crore to ₹1913.97 crore in the financial year of 2024-25. As per the 
recommendations of the committee, the Ministry has already worked out and made 
an action plan to utilize the allocated funds for PMJVK Scheme timely.   Due to this 
an expenditure of ₹204.28 crore (upto 16.6.2025) has already been incurred under 
the scheme and released to the eligible States/UTs for implementation of projects 
approved under PMJVK. Further, many States/UTs are eligible for release of funds 
and it is expected that remaining ₹809 crore may be released to them during 2nd 
quarter. 
With a vision to usher the digitization of the scheme for effective monitoring 
and evaluation of works taken up at the grassroots level, the Ministry has also 
introduced new modules i.e. QPR reports, Drop module, UC module, big ticket 
projects module etc. in the PMJVK Portal. A two day’s National Workshop was also 
held on 07.05.2025 & 08.05.2025, in which States/UTs/CGOs were given hands-on 
training for effective utilization of these newly developed modules of PMJVK Portal. 
Further, a dedicated PMU team of PMJVK also deployed for regular monitoring 
and frequent communication with the respective Nodal Officers of the States/ UTs/ 
CGOs. These States/UTs/CGOs are also given technical & administrative support to 
ensure timely resolution of all their queries.

Recommendation (Para No. 2.6) 
The Committee note that the actual expenditure of the Ministry of Minority Affairs 
has gone down considerably during previous years. The Ministry could spend only ₹ 
837.68 crore and ₹ 1,032.65 crore out of ₹ 2,612.66 (RE) crore and ₹ 2,608.93 
(RE) crore during the year 2022-23 and 2023-24. The situation did not improve in 
2024-25 as the Ministry were able to spend only ₹919.10 crore out of budgetary 
allocation of ₹ 3,183.24 crore (BE) by 31 December, 2024. The Committee have 
been apprised that the Ministry have not been able to spend the budgetary 
allocation as several Schemes such as Free Coaching and Allied Scheme, Nai 
Udaan, Scheme of Providing Education in Madrasas/ Minorities (SPEMM), etc, have 
been discontinued and PM-VIKAS Scheme launched in 2023-24 did not initiate. 
Further, the amount allocated during 2022-23 to 2024-25 under various Scholarship 
Schemes of the Ministry could not be spent because these Schemes are under 
consideration for approval since 2022-23 as they are being harmonised with the 
Schemes of other line Ministries, viz. Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs. The Committee strongly believe that the Ministry of 
Minority Affairs are making all efforts to achieve the mission of the Ministry by 
streamlining and strengthening the prevailing System so that the deserving 
Minorities can avail the benefits of the Schemes and the funds are not misused. The 
Committee feel that the steps taken by the Ministry were necessary in order to 
harmonize the system with the welfare Schemes of Ministry of Social Justice & 
Empowerment and Ministry of Tribal Affairs and hope that these steps will improve 
the implementation of the Schemes and enhance the socio-economic condition of 
six notified minority communities in the country. Since the Ministry of Minority 
Affairs are in process of streamlining/strengthening the prevailing System, the 
Committee expect that the necessary approvals will be obtained by the Ministry at 
the earliest so that the allocated Budget of ₹ 3,350.00 crore for 2025-26 is fruitfully 
utilised. The Committee, therefore, recommend the Ministry of Minority Affairs to 
vigorously pursue with the concerned Ministries/ Departments for the pending 
approvals and keep the administrative machinery of the Ministry ready for 
immediate implementation of the Schemes as soon as they are approved. 
 
 


12 
 
Reply of the Government 
The Observations of Hon’ble Committee have been noted for compliance.  
 
Under the Nai Udaan scheme, financial support was provided to candidates 
who qualify in the preliminary examinations conducted by Union Public Service 
Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), State Public Service 
Commissions (SPSCs). No other Ministry / Department provide such support to their 
beneficiaries. Hence, in order to align with the practices and schemes followed by 
other Ministries and to attain uniformity, it had been decided to discontinue this 
scheme w.e.f. 2022-23. 
Under Free Coaching and Allied Schemes (Naya Savera), coaching were 
provided to students from minority community to empower and prepare them for 
competitive and entrance examinations. The New Education Policy 2020 does not 
support coaching programs; thus, the Ministry decide to discontinue the scheme 
w.e.f. 2022-23. 
Scholarship: 
After taking cognizance of media reports in the year 2020 regarding 
siphoning of Scholarship fund, the matter was referred to the Central Bureau of 
Investigation. Also, States were shared suggestive measures to incorporate in 
implementation of Scholarship Schemes. 
In the year 2023, a third party evaluation study, conducted by this Ministry, 
highlighted some irregularities, wherein out of sampled 1,572 institutes, 830 
institutes were found to be either fake/ partially fake or non-operational. Observing 
the seriousness of the issue, Aadhaar based bio-metric authentication drive was 
conducted in which about 27 lakh students and verifying officials were to be 
verified. After the drive, about 18.87 lakh students were finally verified for the year 
2022-23. Subsequently, in order to make the system more robust, Aadhaar 
Payment Bridge System has been introduced for disbursement of scholarships.  In 
the year 2024-25, a special drive for verification was held in the North Eastern 
States wherein, fake beneficiaries and verifying authorities were recorded. These 
were for the academic year 2021-22 and 2022-23. This exhibited that due diligence 
was not done by the States in implementing the Scholarship Schemes of Minority 
Affairs in some institutes. States have filed FIRs in this regard. Besides, the States 
have been given additional list of suspicious institutes (based on red flags 
generated by National Informatics Centers- National Scholarship Portal) to get them 
verified/ inspected and take punitive actions against fraudulent elements. However, 
reports from the states are still awaited. In order to prevent duplicity of benefits, 
MoMA has also asked all the States to integrate their State Scholarship Portals with 
the National Scholarship Portal so that de-duplication can be done and one-student 

13 
 
one-benefit could be ensured. However, the efforts by the States are yet to take a 
logical shape. In such circumstances, approval of Schemes could not be accorded 
by the competent authority and thus, the Ministry could not spend allocated funds 
under the three Scholarship Schemes. This Ministry endeavors to implement these 
schemes at the earliest.

Recommendation (Para No. 3.10) 
 The Committee find that the actual expenditure under various educational 
Schemes was very insignificant in comparison to the budgetary allocation as several 
Schemes such as Free Coaching and Allied Scheme, Nai Udaan, Scheme of 
Providing Education in Madrasas/Minorities (SPEMM), Maulana Azad National 
Fellowship, etc. have been discontinued and Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship 
Schemes are pending for approval since 2022-23. The Committee feel that since 
the Schemes discontinued were in operation for several years, their sudden 
discontinuation would deprive the targeted beneficiaries from the benefits of these 
Schemes. The Committee have no doubt about the intention of the Ministry but 
strongly desire that the substitutes of these Schemes even if at all available 
elsewhere, the beneficiaries should be made aware of such Schemes by publicizing 
them. Further, the Ministry should take necessary measures for the Scholarship 
Schemes pending for approval as the financial aid provided under these Schemes is 
very important and any more delay will adversely affect the educational prospects 
of the students belonging to Minority Communities. The Committee may like to be 
apprised of the initiatives taken by the Ministry of Minority Affairs in getting the 
approvals of these Schemes.

After taking cognizance of media reports in the year 2020 regarding 
siphoning of Scholarship fund, the matter was referred to the Central Bureau of

In the year 2023, a third party evaluation study, conducted by this Ministry,

institutes were found to be either fake/ partially fake or non-operational. Observing 
the seriousness of the issue, Aadhaar based bio-metric authentication drive was 
conducted in which about 27 lakh students and verifying officials were to be 
verified. After the drive, about 18.87 lakh students were finally verified for the year 

14 
 
2022-23. Subsequently, in order to make the system more robust, Aadhaar 
Payment Bridge System has been introduced for disbursement of scholarships. 
In the year 2024-25, a special drive for verification was held in the North 
Eastern States wherein, fake beneficiaries and verifying authorities were recorded. 
These were for the academic year 2021-22 and 2022-23. This exhibited that due 
diligence was not done by the States in implementing the Scholarship Schemes of 
Minority Affairs in some institutes. States have filed FIRs in this regard. Besides, the 
States have been given additional list of suspicious institutes (based on red flags 
generated by National Informatics Centers- National Scholarship Portal) to get them 
verified/ inspected and take punitive actions against fraudulent elements. However,

In order to prevent duplicity of benefits, MoMA has also asked all the States

socially, educationally and economically marginalized sections of the society including 
Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, De-notified and Nomadic Tribes (DNTs),

Transgenders, Victims of Alcoholism and Substance abuse. The vision of the Department 
is to build an inclusive society wherein members of the target groups can lead productive, 
safe and dignified lives with adequate support for their growth and development.

2.8 In view of the surrender of funds during the Year 2024-25, the Committee asked, whether 
any assessment has been done with regard to the allocation of budget on each scheme. The 
Department submitted vide their written reply that the Department of Social Justice and 
Empowerment undertakes assessment and review of budgetary allocation under its schemes to 
ensure that implementation does not suffer for want of funds.  
 
(i) Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship for SCs and Others and the Post Matric Scholarship 
Scheme for SC students, which are implemented through DBT mode, States/UTs submit realistic 
targets in their Annual Action Plans. These proposals are appraised every year by the Project 
Appraisal Committee (PAC) under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Department of Social Justice 
and Empowerment, generally in April/May. This appraisal process ensures that allocations are 
based on actual requirement and realistic beneficiary projections.  
(ii) Under SHREYAS-SCs, no separate assessment with regard to allocation of budget on 
each component has been undertaken; however, allocations are made keeping in view past 
expenditure trends and ongoing commitments to ensure smooth implementation during FY 
2025–26.  
 
(iii) Under PM-AJAY, the total outlay for the period 2021–22 to 2025–26 has been approved 
by the Expenditure Finance Committee. Allocation among components is governed by approved 
scheme guidelines and clearly defined criteria. As per the guidelines, up to 50% of the total 
allocation is earmarked for the Adarsh Gram component based on actual requirement, up to 5% 

14  
for administration, monitoring and evaluation, and up to 2% for construction of hostels in Central 
institutions, with the remaining funds allocated to States/UTs under the Grants-in-Aid component. 
Savings under any component are redistributed to other components or States/UTs against 
viable proposals, subject to scheme guidelines. These provisions ensure balanced and need-
based allocation so that the scheme does not suffer due to lack of funds. 
 
(iv) Under SRESHTA, no separate assessment exercise has been undertaken for allocation 
of budget; however, allocations are made in accordance with approved scheme guidelines and 
projected admissions to ensure continuity of support.  
 
(v) Under AVYAY, the Department regularly reviews scheme performance and coverage to 
ensure adequate budgetary provisioning. Over the last five years, the number of Senior Citizen 
Homes supported under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens has increased from 607 
to 705, reflecting enhanced coverage. Under Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, the number of assistive 
aids and devices has been expanded from 8 to 17, increasing beneficiary outreach. Periodic 
National Review Conferences with States/UTs and independent evaluation by NITI Aayog 
through the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) also guide budget 
projections and strengthen implementation to prevent any shortfall in allocation; and 
 
(vi) Under NAMASTE, the budget is proposed based on yearly provisions approved under 
the SFC/EFC process, and regular reviews are conducted to monitor expenditure across 
components to ensure adequate provisioning. 
 
2.9 On being enquired with regard to the measures being taken to ensure that the funds 
allocated do not remain idle so that the targeted sections do not suffer due to procedural lapses 
at the level of States/UT Governments, the Committee were informed by the Department of 
Social Justice and Empowerment vide their written reply that has stated that: 
 
“Yes, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment has evolved systems to 
ensure that funds allocated under its schemes do not remain idle and that the targeted 
sections do not suffer due to procedural lapses at the level of States/UT Governments. The 
mechanisms introduced in recent years have yielded positive results in improving 
transparency, accountability and timely utilisation of funds.” 
 
(i) Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship for SCs and Others and the Post Matric 
Scholarship for SC students, the schemes are open-ended and demand-
driven for all eligible students of recognised institutions across India. 
Applications are invited through a designated online portal and the Central 
share is released through DBT directly into Aadhaar-seeded bank 
accounts of beneficiaries. States/UTs are responsible for inviting 
applications and verification through their established mechanisms. The 
DBT framework and portal-based processing minimise the possibility of 
funds remaining idle and ensure that eligible students receive scholarships 
directly.  

15  
 
(ii) Under SHREYAS-SCs, being a Central Sector Scheme, there is no 
State/UT-wise allocation of funds. Funds are released centrally based on 
approved proposals and ongoing commitments, thereby reducing the risk 
of idle balances at the State level and ensuring timely support to 
beneficiaries.  
 
(iii) Under PM-AJAY, since FY 2021–22, ₹ 1712.56 crore has been released 
under the Adarsh Gram component and 13,947 villages have been 
declared as Adarsh Gram. Under the Grant-in-Aid component, ₹1527.43 
crore has been provided to 2,48,570 beneficiaries, and ₹ 177.63 crore has 
been sanctioned for 90 hostels covering 10,649 beneficiaries. The 
introduction of the SNA SPARSH system, PFMS-based monitoring and 
regular review meetings has helped reduce idle funds and improve 
transparency. The scheme has been onboarded on SNA-SPARSH with 
effect from 01 July 2025, enabling just-in-time releases and preventing 
accumulation of unspent balances. Releases are linked to utilisation and 
compliance, thereby safeguarding beneficiary interests.  
 
(iv) Under SRESHTA, funds are released directly to selected schools/NGOs 
under the Central Sector framework. Releases are linked to compliance 
with scheme guidelines, inspections and submission of Utilization 
Certificates, which minimises the risk of funds remaining idle and ensures 
that students continue to receive support without disruption.  
 
 
(v) Under AVYAY, the introduction of the SNA-SPARSH fund flow system, 
mandatory submission of Utilization Certificates, inspection-based 
releases and periodic review meetings with States/UTs have significantly 
improved fund utilisation. Releases to States/UTs and NGOs are linked to 
implementation progress, compliance verification and physical 
inspections. In cases of delay at the State/UT level, the Department 
undertakes continuous follow-up and provides handholding support so that 
benefits to senior citizens are not adversely affected.  
 
(vi) Under NAMASTE, centralised procurement of PPE kits for sanitation 
workers and safety devices for Emergency Response Sanitation Units is 
undertaken and supplies are delivered to States/UTs for onward 
distribution. This centralised model reduces delays and ensures that 
beneficiaries receive equipment in a timely manner. The mechanisms 
introduced in recent years have yielded positive results in improving 
transparency, accountability and timely utilisation of funds.

prescribed procedure for allocation/ disbursement of funds to the beneficiaries, the Committee

accounts. These procedural issues have contributed to delays in fund utilisation during FY 
2025–26. The Department has been regularly conducting review meetings, providing

compliance.”

2.13 The Committee appreciate that the BE has been continuously increased over the 
last few years. From ₹ 12847 cr in 2023-24 it has now been increased to ₹ 13687.59 cr for 
the year 2026-27.The Committee however are not pleased to note that the Department of 
Social Justice and Empowerment has not been able to spend the allocated amount over 
all  these years. Even in the year 2025-26, ₹7317.95 crore only has been spent out of the 
Revised Estimates of ₹11402.74 crore. The Department still has a balance of almost 30 
percent of the Revised Estimates, even though the financial year 2025–26 is about to end. 
The Committee are also concerned to note that the Budget Estimates is invariably reduced 
by almost 25 to 30 percent every year at the time of the revision of estimates. The 
Committee do not find this to be a good indicator with regard to the performance of the 
Department. The hurdles in implementing Schemes, due to which the estimates are to be 
revised downwards or the funds remain unspent, should not be a recurring feature. These 
issues need to be resolved within a specific time period. The Committee, therefore, expect 
that the factors such as onboarding of States/UTs on SNA-SPARSH, submission of 
Utilization Certificates, release of matching shares by the State Governments, etc., will be 
sorted out in this financial year so that there is no more hinderance in the implementation 
of the Schemes. The Committee are optimistic with regard to the changes proposed to 
Expenditure Finance Committee of the Ministry of Finance in the Schemes of the 
Department of Social justice and expect that once approved for next financial cycle of 
2026-27 to 2030-31 will not only benefit but also boost the morale of the deprived sections 
of society. 
2.14 The Committee find that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
surrendered ₹2345.1897 crore out of ₹10309.00 crore sanctioned for the Scheduled Caste 
Division in 2024-25. Similarly, the Department surrendered ₹540.3672 crore out of 
₹2064.41 crore sanctioned to the Backward Classes Division and ₹79.5324 crore out of 
₹412.4600 crore sanctioned for the Social Defence Division. The Committee are unable to 

18  
comprehend the reasons due to which large portion of the allocation had to be 
surrendered in respect of the Schemes meant for the poorest of the poor section of the 
Society i.e., SCs, OBCs, EBCs and DNTs. Further, nearly 20 to 25 percent of the budget 
allocated for Top Class Education for SCs and Top Class School and College schemes 
for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs was surrendered by the Department. The Committee cannot 
draw any other conclusion than that the surrender of funds can take place only when 
either there is no proper assessment or the Implementing agencies are not strictly 
implementing the Schemes. The justification provided that the Department was in receipt 
of fewer proposals, delays in submission of replies, inadequate number of eligible 
admissions is not convincing to the Committee. The Committee are of the firm opinion 
that in a country where a large proportion of the population is young and requires proper 
education and skill development, the funds allocated should not remain unutilized due to 
the petty hindrances which can be resolved with little efforts. The Committee expect that 
the Department will take due care to ensure that educational schemes do not suffer and 
that problems arising in implementation are resolved immediately without any loss of 
time. 
2.15 The Committee are happy to note that the Budget Estimates have been 
successively increasing every year from ₹12847.02 crore in 2023–24 to ₹13687.59 crore 
for the year 2026–27. The Committee are however not happy to note that, the percentage 
allocation for the department of the total budget of Central Government has declined from 
0.29% in 2023– 24 to 0.26% in 2026–27. In the current scenario, when the Government of 
India is working towards the welfare of SCs, OBCs, EBCs, DNTs, etc., the Committee feel 
that the annual share of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment should 
increase rather than decrease. Though the decline seems to be marginal. The Committee 
feel it is a matter of grave concern and the Department should take it up with the Ministry 
of Finance. 
   Also, the Committee have no doubt on the sincerity of the Government but strongly feel 
that there is a lack of coherence between the Central and State Governments due to which 
there is under-utilization of Budgetary Estimates, resulting into surrender of funds. The 
Committee note that right steps are being taken by the Government for the welfare of the 
deprived sections of society but the hurdles in implementing is perhaps due to 
deficiencies in the mechanisms developed for smooth implementation. The Committee 
are, therefore, not happy to note that the same problems continue to recur and the 

19  
budgetary allocations continues to remain underutilized year after year even though the 
Department of Social Justice and Empowerment promises the Committee every year that 
it will fully utilise the funds allocated in the next financial year. The Committee’s main 
concern is that the citizens eligible for the benefits of the Scheme meant to improve their 
life are not deprived for the inefficiencies of others. The Committee hope that the 
Budgetary Allocation for 2026–27 will be fully utilized with minimal revisions and that the 
Department will take sufficient measures to break this vicious cycle. The Committee 
would like to be informed in this regard.

POST MATRIC SCHOLARSHIP FOR SCHEDULED CASTES 
 
The Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste (SC) students is a Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme, implemented by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
(DoSJE) through State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. This Scheme is currently 
in the final year of the existing Finance Commission cycle (2020-21 to 2025-26) till 2025-26. In 
view of the completion of the current cycle, the process of revising the Scheme guidelines for the 
next cycle (2026-27 to 2030-31) has been initiated. The Post-Matric Scholarship are awarded by 
the Government of the State/UT to which the applicant actually belongs i.e. permanently settled 
or domiciled. Parent/Guardian's income should not exceed ₹ 2.5 lakh per annum. The objective 
of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the Scheduled Caste students and to 
appreciably increase the Gross Enrollment Ratio of SC students in higher education with a focus 
on those from the poorest households. It is the endeavor of the Government to raise the GER of 
SCs in higher education from 23.0 % to the national average.

3.13 The Government provide financial assistance to Scheduled Caste students to 
increase the Gross Enrolment Ratio of SC students in higher education through the Post 
Matric Scholarship Scheme. In this regard, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
spent ₹5476.22 crore in 2023-24, ₹5581.52 crore in 2024-25 and ₹4934.67 crore in 2025-26 by 
24 March, 2026. Similarly, the number of students provided scholarships in 2023-24 was 
47.38 lakhs, 48.04 lakhs for 2024-25 and 36.07 lakhs for 2025-26 in March, 2026. The 
Committee are not able to understand how the Department is going to enhance the Gross 
Enrolment Ratio of SC students in higher education when the actual expenditure and the 
number of beneficiaries have actually decreased in 2025-26. In fact, the achievement (36.07 
lakhs) vis-à-vis the target (76.55 lakhs) is very poor. The Committee feel that the objective 
of the Department to achieve a higher enrolment ratio can only be achieved when there is a 
substantial increase in the number of beneficiaries and actual expenditure. The Committee 
would like the Department to take appropriate action so that the number of beneficiaries 
increase, such as, publicizing the Scheme, obtaining feedback from the students, etc. The 
Committee would like to be informed of the concrete measures taken by the Department to 
enhance the number of beneficiaries. 
3.14 The Committee note that the target for beneficiaries is fixed on the basis of the Annual 
Action Plan received in April/May from the States/UTs. However, the Committee find that the 
scholarship is released in the next academic year as the State/UT Governments are not able 
to complete the formalities of processing of application as scheduled. The Committee feel 
that the scholarship for an academic year should be disbursed in the same academic year 
so that a student is able to use the scholarship, fruitfully. The Committee has time and again 
recommended that appropriate measures be taken in this regard, however, the practice 
remains the same. The Committee are happy to be informed that the guidelines are under 

26  
revision and the scholarship will be disbursed in the first four to five months of the 
academic year. The Committee hope that the Department of Social Justice and 
Empowerment will leave no stone unturned to ensure that the scholarship is disbursed 
timely and the revised guidelines will yield the desired results from the academic year 2026-
27. 
3.15 The Committee observe that the number of beneficiaries has increased marginally 
between 2022-23 and 2024-25 but the number of beneficiaries has substantially gone down 
in Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West 
Bengal during the period 2022-23 to 2024-25. The Committee also find that approximately 
40% of the target fixed for 2025-26 has only been achieved till the time of examination of 
Demand for Grants (2026-27). The Committee are not able to comprehend the reasons for 
the decline in the number of beneficiaries and the factors that have become a hindrance in 
achieving the target particularly in the context when the population of the country is 
increasing. The Committee would especially like to draw the attention of the Department 
with regard to the States where the number of beneficiaries has gone down. The Committee 
are of the view that schemes meant for deprived sections of society cannot be left entirely 
at the mercy of the Implementing Agencies, Governments need to take control of the 
Schemes. The Central Government instead of making the State/UT Governments entirely 
responsible for implementing the Scheme, the Committee feel that the Department should 
also be held responsible in case the Schemes are not being implemented, meticulously. The 
Committee would therefore like the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment to take 
necessary action in this regard.

4.38 The Committee note that the Annual Expenditure under the National Fellowship for 
SC Scheme was more than the Budget Estimates in the years 2023-24 and 2024-25 and is 
likely to exceed the Budget Estimate again in 2025-26 as they have been able to spend 
₹204.04 crore against the Budget Estimate of ₹212.00 crore at the time of examination. The 
Committee find that the target of 2000 fellowships fixed at the inception of the scheme in 
2005-06 has remained the same even in subsequent years. The Committee does not find 
any justification for not increasing the target for more than 20 years and thereby restricting 
students from availing the benefits of the scheme to undertake advanced studies and 

42  
research leading to PhD degrees. The Committee believe that increasing the number of 
fellowships under this scheme would provide greater opportunities to under-privileged 
candidates in addition to those qualifying the cut-off marks notified by UGC-CSIR for NET-
JRF. Even after the several evaluations of the scheme conducted over the year, the 
Committee are surprised that no recommendation for enhancement of fellowship numbers 
has been made till date. The Committee are of the view that the department should analyze 
the number of applications received under the scheme in the last three years. If the number 
of applications received each year is increasing then it justifies the need to increase the 
number of fellowships so that a larger number of applicants get an opportunity to avail the 
fellowship. It is also a fact that several students do not pursue advanced studies due to lack 
of financial assistance. Keeping in view the educational backwardness of a large section of 
the SC population, the Committee strongly believe that the number of fellowships need to 
be enhanced so that the scheme accommodates more aspiring students. The Committee 
would like to be informed of the action taken in this regard. 
 
4.39 The Committee are happy to note that the beneficiaries of the PM- CARES Children 
Scheme have been included in the free coaching scheme for SCs and OBCs from 2024-25. 
All beneficiaries of the PM- CARES Children Scheme are eligible to avail the benefits of the 
scheme irrespective of income whereas the ceiling of the total family income for SC and 
OBC students is ₹8 lakh per annum. The Committee find that the target fixed for 2023-24 
and 2024-25 could not be achieved even after the inclusion of PM-CARES Children Scheme. 
The requirement for coaching support is well recognized particularly among students 
belonging to the educationally disadvantaged sections of Scheduled Castes and Other 
Backward Classes. It is also well known that the coaching is an expensive affair and 
everybody cannot avail coaching due to its high cost, hence the candidates from Scheduled 
Castes and Other Backward Classes aspiring for coaching cannot avail this facility even if 
the annual income of family is more than ₹ 8 Lakh. The Committee strongly feel that the 
total family income criterion fixed for SC and OBC students may be one of the major hurdles 
preventing candidates from these categories from availing the benefits. The Committee also 
does not understand the reason for fixing a target of 7000, which is double the previous 
target, particularly when the target fixed earlier is not being achieved. The Committee desire 
that the family income ceiling should be re-examined so that a large number of candidates 
can avail the facility and scheme becomes more effective. 
 

43  
4.40 The Committee appreciate that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
provide scholarships to meritorious SC students for pursuing studies beyond the 12th class 
in the selected 274 premier Institutions and Top 100 National Institutional Ranking 
Framework under the Top Class Education scheme. The Committee note that no target will 
be fixed from 2026-27 onwards and scholarships will be provided to all eligible SC students 
but subject to the availability of budget. The Committee feel that non-fixing of target become 
meaningless if the budget is not appropriately enhanced as the budget available for 2026-
2027 is ₹120 crore whereas actual expenditure incurred in 2024-2025 was ₹103.26 crore. The 
Committee are of the view, that the Scheme will give much benefit to the candidates if the 
Budget is  enhanced to accommodate all applicants getting admission in selected 
Institutions. Hence, the changes proposed, if implemented, may prove superfluous unless 
the budget is substantially enhanced, as the available budget can only accommodate a 
limited number of students and not all eligible candidates. The Committee also find that the 
family income ceiling of ₹8 lakh fixed in 2020-21 may also be one of the constraints for 
students intending to avail scholarship under the scheme. The Committee would also like 
to draw the attention to the fact that the Department is spending the allocated budget 
despite receiving less applications than the target fixed for previous years. This sufficiently 
indicates that the income eligibility criteria need to be revised to attract more applicants, as 
it has been more than five years since the ceiling was revised from ₹6 lakh to ₹8 lakh. The 
students with the income eligibility limit of ₹8 lakh may still not be in a position to bear the 
burden of the high fees charged by such institutions. The Committee are sure that the 
Department will understand and take substantive measures to enhance the income ceiling 
and annual budget to extend the benefits of the scheme to the maximum number of needy 
candidates securing admission in to premier selected Institutions.  
 
4.41 The Committee are happy to note that the slots of National Overseas Scholarships 
for SCs have been increased from 125 to 250 from the year 2026-27 based on the 
recommendations of this Committee’s report in march 2025. Simultaneously, it is surprising 
to note that the Budget Estimate for 2026-27 is same as 2025-26.  The Committee are unable 
to understand how the Department will provide scholarship to the students if the demand 
for 250 slots is received in 2026-27 in the limited Budget meant for 125 slots only. The 
Committee also find that the Overseas Scholarships offered by some States is more 
preferred over National Overseas Scholarship as these State Governments provides the 
facility of direct transfer of scholarship amounts to students’ bank accounts and there is no 

44  
restriction to return to India. The Committee believe that all efforts should be made to make 
the scheme more popular among students and necessary changes should be made in 
provisions that are becoming impediments in making the scheme attractive to candidates.  
   The Committee observed that the slots earmarked for Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-
Nomadic Tribes, Landless Agricultural Laborers and Traditional Artisans have remained 
unutilised over the years due to financial constraints. The Committee recommend that the 
government find out ways and means to fill the earmarked slots this year. 
The Committee are deeply concerned with the outcome of this Scheme as the Department 
may not find sufficient students to fill the available slots for 2026-27 unless the restrictions 
applicable are waived off and the income eligibility criteria is amended. The Committee 
strongly feel that the scheme needs to be exhaustively re-examined with respect to income 
ceiling limit, budgetary allocation, etc. and revised in the interest of the targeted sections 
of the society.  The Committee would like to be informed of the action taken in this regard. 
 
4.42 The Committee are concerned to note the poor physical and financial performance of 
the scheme of ‘Free Coaching for SCs and OBCs’ over the years. The objective of the 
scheme is to provide coaching of good quality for economically disadvantage SCs & OBCs 
to enable them to appear in competitive examination and/or for securing admission in 
reputed technical and professional higher education institution. Out of the BE of ₹ 47 cr in 
2023-24 AE was only ₹ 7.76 cr BE was reduced to ₹ 35 cr in 2024-25 still AE was ₹ 17.68 cr 
only. Similarly in 2025-26, BE was further downgraded to ₹ 20 cr & AE was only ₹ 7.11 cr. 
The physical performance has been equally poor as vis-à-vis the target of 3500 achievement 
has only been 223 in 2023-24, 2136 in 2024-25 & 431 in 2025-26. 
   The Committee are not satisfied with the explanation given by the department for this poor 
performance such as limited participation by the Central Universities and delayed 
proposals. The performance has remained poor inspite of changes introduced by the 
Department over the years such as making Dr. Ambedkar Foundation as the Central Nodal 
Agency. The Committee note that the proposal for 16th Finance Committee cycle includes 
inclusion of state Universities and introduction of student centric mode for wider coverage. 
The Committee desire that these changes be made effective at the earliest to ensure that 
the BE of ₹ 20 cr for this purpose for the year 2026-27 is fully utilized.

all eligible villages are expected to be developed as Adarsh Grams in the country, the Department 
of Social Justice and Empowerment vide written reply stated that: 
 
“Community development works are being undertaken such as internal approach road, 
solid and liquid waste management infrastructure, soak pit, street light etc. are carried out 
in SC dominated villages. These developmental works are according to Village 
Development Plans based on need assessment, with emphasis on convergence of Central 
and State schemes and utilisation of gap-filling funds under PM-AJAY for infrastructure 
needs that cannot be met through other schemes. The Department added that a village 
selected under the Adarsh Gram component is declared as an “Adarsh Gram” once it 
achieves Open Defecation Free (ODF) status and secures a minimum score of 70 out of 
100 on the 50 prescribed socio-economic Monitorable Indicators. As and when a village 
fulfils the above criteria the State Government declares it as Adarsh Gram. Therefore, 
declaration of villages as Adarsh Gram is an ongoing process. 5,510 villages have score 
more than 70 out of 100 and are likely to be declared as Adarsh Grams by the State 
Government by the end of this Financial Year. The department continuously monitors and 
urges State Governments through regular review meetings, field visits and chintan shivirs 
to declare all the villages as Adarsh Grams.”

5.13 Its objective is to reduce poverty of the SC communities by generation of additional 
employment opportunities through skill development, income generating schemes and other 
initiatives.

State Governments/ UTs and hence, the current status of the projects have been sought 
by the State Governments vide letter dated 19.02.2026”. 
 
5.15 On being asked whether the objective of Grants-in-Aid scheme is being achieved, the 
Department of Social Justice and Empowerment stated in their written reply that: 
 
“The objective of the Grants-in-Aid component is to promote the socio-economic 
empowerment of Scheduled Castes through district and State-level projects tailored to 
local needs. The component aims to increase the income of the target population by 
supporting comprehensive livelihood projects that include income-generating schemes,

completion of construction, which shall not exceed the prescribed maximum period. The 
Ministry does not bear any time or cost overruns of infrastructure projects, and any delay in

5.20 The Committee are worried with regard to the expenditure incurred during 2023-24 
and 2024-25 under the Scheme PM-AJAY as the Department of Social Justice and 
Empowerment was able to spend only about 25 to 30 percent of the Budgetary allocation 
during these years. The situation has further deteriorated as only ₹244.61 crore has been 
spent till February 2026. The Committee have been time and again informed that delays in 
the implementation of the SNA system, pending utilisation certificates, high SNA balances 
with States/UTs, etc., have adversely affected the Scheme. The Committee are unable to 
understand the reasons for the recurrence for such problems year after year or should the 
Committee conclude that there is no solution to these issues. The Committee feel that the 
Department presents the same problem differently every time at the time of Examination of 
Demands for Grants. This time the Committee have been informed that due to the 
involvement of various Departments/Organisations at the State/UT level, mapping under the 
Financial Management Information System could not be completed at this stage due to 
which there was delay in the clearance of bills. Again, the Committee is not satisfied with 
this version as the Scheme is in existence since 2021-22 and the problem presented this 
year may have been faced by the Department during earlier years too, hence, the 
Department should have sorted out this long time back. The Committee would appreciate if 
the hurdles highlighted in 2025-26 do not recur in 2026- 27 and the expenditure of the budget 
allocated for 2026-27 is fully utilized. The Committee recommend that the Department 
resolves issues hampering the Scheme in a time bound manner for the smooth 

52  
operationalization of the Scheme for the welfare of targeted sections of the society. The 
Committee also emphasize that the new provisions with respect to the Scheme proposed 
to the Expenditure Finance Committee are approved at the earliest so that the scheme do 
not suffer in 2026-27. 
 
5.21 Under ‘Adarsh Gram’ Scheme, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
has spent between 25 to 35 percent of the total budgetary allocation during 2023-24 and 
2024-25 and only ₹81.52 crore out of the ₹1070.00 crore budget estimated for the year 2025-
26. As per the scheme, a selected village is declared as an ‘Adarsh Gram’ once it achieves 
open defecation free status and secures a minimum score of 70 out of 100 on the 50 
prescribed socio-economic indicators. The Committee note that 47357 villages have been 
identified across the country under the Scheme but only 13,947 villages have been declared 
as ‘Adarsh Grams’ by State Governments since 2021-22.  As informed by the Department 
5510 villages are likely to be declared ‘Adarsh Grams’ by the State Governments in the 
current financial year. The Committee are surprised to find that so many villages still do not 
qualify to be declared as “Adarsh Gram” after so many years of India’s independence. The 
Committee desire that the Scheme is meticulously implemented so that the villages are 
open Defecation Free and the basic amenities such as internal approach roads, solid and 
liquid waste management infrastructure, soak pits, street lights, etc., are provided in a time 
bound manner as promised under the Scheme. The Committee would appreciate if all the 
47357 villages identified are declared ‘Adarsh Gram’ in a year or so and the infrastructure 
stipulated under the Scheme is made available in all the villages by next Financial Cycle. 
The Committee would like to be informed of the steps taken in this regard. 
 
5.22 The Committee observe that the funds allocated under the Grants- Aid Scheme during 
2023-24 and 2024-25 remained under-utilised and the situation did not improve much in 
2025-26 as the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment has been able to spend only 
₹156.77 crore out of the Budget Estimate of ₹920.20 cr. It may therefore, be concluded that 
the Department has been able to spend approximately 35% of the Budgetary allocation since 
2023-24.  The Committee also note that the Department has sanctioned 1785 projects under 
the perspective plans for three years and the status of the Projects sanctioned under Plan 
is not available with the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment. The Committee 
feel that the scheme launched with the objective of reducing poverty among SC 
communities by generating additional employment opportunities through skill development 

53  
and other income-generating activities has not picked up been able to maintain the required 
momentum. The Committee therefore desire that the Department should make efforts to 
identify the problem areas and find the solutions so that the scheme gains momentum in 
achieving the income-generating initiative to effectively address the problem of poverty 
among SC communities. The Committee also desire that monitoring mechanism should be 
evolved in the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment so that the updated 
information is available with them for the projects sanctioned.

implemented in two modes, where in Mode-1, fee is reimbursed to Private Residential schools 
affiliated to CBSE/State Boards for providing high quality residential education to meritorious SC 
students. Under Mode-ll, Grant-in-Aid is provided to the NGOs/VOs for running and maintenance 
of the projects of Residential/Non-Residential schools and Hostels for SC students.

PRE-MATRIC SCHOLARSHIPS 
 
7.5 The objective of Pre-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT students (who are not 
covered under SC, ST or OBC) is welfare and motivation to the children of these categories by 
providing financial assistance at pre-matriculation or secondary stage. Scholarship under the 
Scheme will be available for studies in India only. The Salient Features of the scheme are as 
follows: 
 
(i) The scheme is implemented through respective State Governments/ UTs. 
(ii) The scholarship will be provided for students studying in class IXth and Xth on a full-
time basis in Government School only. 
(iii) Parents /guardians income from all sources does not exceed Rs.2,50,000/- per 
annum.  
(iv) The students shall be given a consolidated academic allowance of Rs. 4000/- per 
annum.  

62  
(v) The scheme will be implemented and administered in accordance with the procedure 
laid down by the State Govts. /UT Administration in this regard.  
(vi) The concerned State Governments and Union Territory Administrations will lay 
down   the detailed procedure for selection of students. 
(vii) The award once made will be payable until the student passes Class Xth, subject to 
satisfactory academic performance and attendance of 75% in every academic year.  
(viii) The scholarship portals would remain open throughout the year so that all eligible 
students can register for the Freeship Card and apply for the scholarships. 
(ix) The entire scholarship amount - both from the State and Central Government - 
including the academic allowance and disability allowance, if any, is paid directly into 
the account of the students or parents only through DBT preferably through an 
Aadhaar Based Payment System (Aadhaar Payment Bridge-AePS). 
(x) There is a 60: 40 sharing ratio between the Centre and States. For North Eastern 
States and for the states of Uttarakhand and Himanchal Pradesh the sharing ratio is 
90:10. For UTs without legislatures, 100% funds is provided by Centre. 
(xi) At least 5% students with disabilities should be covered for grant of the scholarships. 
(xii) 30% of the beneficiaries should be reserved for girl students.

feedback prior to budget fixation is not separately published.”

“Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship for OBC students have generally been attributed to 
factors such as delayed submission of incomplete or incorrect proposal as per scheme 
guidelines, Aadhaar seeding and bank account validation issues, late release of 
matching State share in some cases, and lower-than-anticipated eligible enrolment. In 
certain States/UTs, procedural delays, verification backlogs and technical glitches also 
affected timely disbursement. Migration to Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) systems initially

of SNA-SPARSH (Particularly for 2025-26) challenges. To address these issues, 
States/UTs and implementing agencies have strengthened online verification 
mechanisms, chintan shivirs, national level and regional level review meetings, 
conducted awareness drives to improve application accuracy, streamlined fund release 
procedures, and ensured timely submission of utilisation certificates. Regular review 
meetings and monitoring dashboards have been introduced to track progress. Capacity-
building of district-level officers and better coordination with banks have also been 
undertaken. These measures are aimed at ensuring optimal utilisation of allocated funds

CONSTRUCTION OF HOSTELS FOR OBC BOYS AND GIRLS 
7.22 The scheme aims at providing hostel facilities to students belonging to socially and 
educationally backward classes, especially from rural areas to enable them to pursue secondary 
and higher education in the Govt. schools, universities, institutions and institutes located at a 
reasonable distance in order to provide them greater access to high quality education. The 
scheme as such mainly targets the students hailing from remote areas and from poor families 
as well who generally discontinue their studies either because no secondary school and college 

70  
is available near their location or due to non-availability of adequate hostel facilities at a 
reasonable cost at places where such educational institutions are located. The Salient features 
of the Scheme are as follows: 
 
(i) The scheme is implemented through respective States/UTs in respect of State 
Universities. For Central University, the grant is given directly to the institution. 
(ii) Agencies eligible for financial assistance under the revised Scheme will be as follows:- 
a) State Government and UT Administrations; 
b) The institution of repute ranked in the latest NIRF rankings of Ministry of 
Education subject to following conditions:- 
- The institution shall provide free of cost land within the campus.  
- The institution shall undertake to complete construction within 24 
months.  
- The institution shall maintain the hostel after construction as per 
standards prescribed.  
- The institution shall agree to provide as many hostel seats to the new 
OBC students as per the sanction order of the hostel. However, this 
additional accommodation shall be regulated in other hostels as well 
to avoid the hostel being designated as 'OBC hostel' exclusively i.e. if 
a hostel with 100 capacity has been sanctioned under this scheme, 
the institution shall provide 100 additional seats to the OBC students, 
but it can be spread over in all other hostels. 
(iii) Agencies eligible for assistance under the Scheme should have clear title and 
possession over the land where the hostel is to be constructed, and will submit 
proposals in the prescribed formats. 
(iv) The cost of construction of hostels for boys has to be shared between the Centre 
and the State in 60:40 ratio (in case of Girls Hostels 90%   of cost will be borne by 
the Central Govt). In case of Union Territories, the Central Assistance shall be 100% 
and for North Eastern States and 02 Himalayan States (Himachal Pradesh and 
Uttarakhand), it shall be 90%.  
(v) For the Institution of repute ranked in the latest NIRF rankings of Ministry of 
Education, Govt. of India, the Central Assistance shall be 100% irrespective of 
regional States.   
(vi) The construction work of the Hostel has to be completed within eighteen months 
from award of work order or two years from the release of 1st installment of Central 
assistance, whichever is earlier. In no case the time will be extended beyond 2 
years.   
(vii)  The cost per hostel seat in different areas are as follows:-   
- North Eastern Region/Himalayan Regions  -   ₹3.50 lakh per seat 
- Rest of country  -    ₹3.00 lakh per seat, or as per the schedule of the rates 

71  
for the concerned State Government, whichever is lower.  
(ix) The amount of grant will be released in 3 installments in 50:45:5 ratio, of which 5% 
grant will be released after completion of the work and occupation of the rooms by 
the OBC Boys and Girls.  
(x) There will be a one-time non-recurring grant of ₹2500/- per seat for providing 
furniture/equipment to the hostels constructed under the Scheme.

7.25 On being asked, the purpose of having separate hostel for OBC students the Department 
of Social Justice and Empowerment submitted vide written reply that: 
 
“The provision of separate hostels for OBC students is primarily intended as a 
supportive measure to improve access to education for students from socially and 
educationally disadvantaged backgrounds, particularly those coming from remote or 
economically weaker families. If seats reserved for OBC remains vacant, it would be 
filled up in following preference:-  
 
(a) De-notified Tribes (DNT) students 
(b) Scheduled Tribes (ST) Students 
(c) Scheduled Caste (SC) Students 
(d) Economically Weaker Section (EWS) Students 
 
The objective is not segregation, but facilitation of safe, affordable accommodation 
where such facilities are otherwise inadequate. Care is taken to ensure that these 
hostels function as part of the larger campus ecosystem, with students participating 
fully in academic, cultural and extracurricular activities alongside their peers. 
Institutions are advised to promote inclusivity and equal opportunity so that no sense 

73  
of isolation or stigma arises. The overall approach is developmental and welfare-
oriented, aimed at strengthening educational participation without compromising 
social integration.” 
 
7.26 On being enquired with regard to assessment was conducted prior to launch of the 
Scheme, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment stated in their written reply that: 
 
“Department of Social Justice and Empowerment undertook preliminary assessments 
of the need for hostel facilities based on the number of eligible students, gaps in 
existing infrastructure, and regional educational backwardness. These assessments 
drew on data from State Governments, enrolment statistics, and demand projections 
for residential facilities for OBC students. While the scheme originally aimed at 
constructing hostels in phases, the timeline for completion varied by project 
depending on availability of land, administrative approvals, tendering processes, and 
release of funds by both Central and State Governments.” 
 
 
 
7.27 On being asked about the norms laid down for constructions of hostels sanctioned along 
with the number of Hostels constructed within the stipulated period including reasons for delay 
and the action taken thereon, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment stated in their 
written reply that: 
 
“Cost norms are prescribed per seat by region and funding is shared between Centre 
and States/UTs (60:40 for boys, 90:10 for girls; 100% for UTs; 90:10 for Central 
institutions), with a mandatory completion period of 18 months from award of work 
order or 2 years from release of central assistance whichever is earlier, and any cost 
escalation due to delay is to be borne by the State/Institute. It has been noted that 
significant delays have occurred in completing sanctioned hostels, with few 
completed within the stipulated timelines and many remaining incomplete due to 
funding flow issues, administrative/approval bottlenecks, land acquisition and 
procurement delays, tendering and contracting slowdowns, and late release of 
matching State share. Detailed State/Institution‑wise sanctioned vs constructed 
numbers and exact reasons for delay are not maintained by the Ministry; however, 
parliamentary responses and audit observations have highlighted delays in several 
State implementations and noted efforts to review progress and improve monitoring. 
States and implementing agencies have been encouraged through official 
communications to expedite execution, ensure timely release of matching share, 
adhere strictly to prescribed timelines, and improve project management to minimise 
further delays and ensure students benefit from the hostel infrastructure.”

TOP CLASS EDUCATION IN COLLEGE  
 
7.30 The objective of the scheme is to recognise and promote quality education amongst 
Students belonging to OBC, EBC and DNT categories by providing full financial support. The 
Scheme will cover OBC/EBC/DNT students for pursuing studies beyond class XII th. The salient 
features of the Scheme are as follows:  
(i) This Scheme is implemented w.e.f. 2023-24  
(ii) The Scheme will operate in all the institutions notified by the Ministry of Social 
Justice and Empowerment for every financial year.  
(iii) All the IIMs / IITs/ IIITs / AIIMSs/ NITs/NIFTs/ NIDs/ Indian Institutes of Hotel 
Management, National Law Universities and other Central Government Institutions 
will be eligible to be included in the Scheme.  
(iv) The list of the ‘Top Class’ Institutions to be covered under the Scheme    along with 
number of scholarship slots will be notified by the Department of Social Justice and 
Empowerment.  
(v) The scholarship, once awarded, will continue till the completion of the course, 
subject to satisfactory performance of the student.  
(vi) The scholarship will be terminated if the student fails to get promoted to the next 
semester/class.  
(vii) The students, who secure admission in the notified institutions, will be awarded 
scholarship to meet the following requirements for  
(a) full tuition fee and non-refundable charges (there will be a ceiling of ₹ 2.00 
lakh per annum per student for private sector institutions and ₹ 3.72 lakhs 
per annum per student for the private sector flying clubs for Commercial 
Pilot Training and Type Rating Courses)  
(b) living expenses to the beneficiary @₹3000/-per month per student

           CHAPTER-VIII 
 
ATAL VAYO ABHYUDAY YOJANA (AVYAY) 
The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE) is the nodal Ministry for the 
welfare of senior citizens. In alignment with the principles of active and healthy ageing and to 
ensure dignified living for the elderly, the Ministry is implementing the umbrella scheme Atal 
Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY). AVYAY seeks to provide comprehensive and integrated 
services through the convergence of various interventions targeted at different aspects of elderly 
welfare ranging from shelter and medical care to assistive devices, helpline services and 
caregiver training. The components under AVYAY are as follows: - 
 
INTEGRATED PROGRAMME FOR SENIOR CITIZENS (IPSRC) 
 
8.2 The objective of the IPSrC is to enhance the quality of life of senior citizens, particularly 
indigent elderly persons, by providing essential amenities such as shelter, food, medical care 
and recreational facilities, while promoting productive and active ageing. Under the scheme, 
financial assistance in the form of grant-in-aid is provided to eligible implementing agencies, 
including NGOs and voluntary organizations, for the operation and maintenance of various 
facilities, including Senior Citizens’ Homes for 25 beneficiaries, Senior Citizens’ Homes for 50 
beneficiaries (male only or combined male and female), Senior Citizens’ Homes exclusively for 
50 elderly women, Continuous Care Homes and homes for senior citizens suffering from 
Alzheimer’s disease or dementia for a minimum of 20 beneficiaries, Regional Resource and 
Training Centers, and Mobile Medicare Units (MMUs) and Physiotherapy Clinics for senior 
citizens. 
 
STATE ACTION PLAN FOR SENIOR CITIZENS (SAPSRC) 
 
8.3 The State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC) is a component of the Atal Vayo 
Abhudaya Yojana (AVYAY) under which financial assistance is provided to States and Union 
Territories to implement state-specific initiatives for the welfare of senior citizens, with a primary 
focus on cataract surgeries for senior citizens, training of geriatric caregivers, awareness 
generation about the scheme, and any other activities considered appropriate by the States/UTs 
to improve the well-being of senior citizens. 
 
RASHTRIYA VAYOSHRI YOJANA (RVY) 
 
8.4 Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) was first announced in the 2015-16 Union Budget 
speech by the finance minister and subsequently launched on 01st April, 2017. The objective of 
the scheme is to provide eligible senior citizens suffering from any of the age-related disability/ 
infirmity, with assisted living devices which can restore near normalcy in their bodily functions, 

81  
overcoming the disability/ infirmity manifested such as low vision, hearing impairment, loss of 
teeth and loco-motor disabilities. 
  
ELDERLINE: NATIONAL HELPLINE FOR SENIOR CITIZENS (NHSC) 
 
8.5 National Helpline for Senior Citizens was dedicated to the Nation on 01st October, 2021 
on the occasion of the International Day of Older Persons, with the toll-free number 14567. 
Elderline operates for 12 hours a day (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM) and provides free information, 
guidance, emotional support and field intervention in cases of abuse, neglect and rescue. The 
National Institute of Social Defence, an autonomous body under MoSJE, is the nodal agency for 
implementation of Elderline across the country. 
 
 
SENIOR CARE AGEING GROWTH ENGINE (SAGE) 
 
8.6 SAGE portal was dedicated to the Nation on 01 October 2021. The scheme aims to 
encourage entrepreneurs and start-ups to develop innovative solutions to address challenges 
faced by the elderly. Under the scheme, Government of India support is provided to start-ups 
through equity participation of up to 49%, with assistance up to ₹1 crore, to promote elder-care 
innovations. 
 
SYSTEM FOR PROVISION OF ELDERCARE IN-HOUSE AND ASSISTED LIVING (PM 
SPECIAL)/ TRAINING OF GERIATRIC CARE GIVERS 
 
8.7 The main objective of the PM Special (Training of Geriatric Care Givers) scheme is to 
bridge the gap in supply and increasing demand in the field of geriatric caregivers so as to 
provide more professional services to the senior citizens and also to create a cadre of 
professional caregivers in the field of geriatrics. The Scheme will ensure sufficient availability of 
dedicated, professionally trained manpower of geriatric caregivers who can attend to diverse 
and dynamic needs of elderly population relating to recreation and holistic well-being. So far, 
35,480 trainees have been imparted training under the scheme.

nutrition, etc.  As per the proposal the Centre and State would be sharing expenditure in 
the ratio of 60:40. The Committee are sure that the measures being proposed would 
enhance the performance of the Scheme in the interest of senior citizens but they are 
apprehensive for the 40% share of State government. The Committee do not want the 
Scheme to suffer for want of funds from State Governments. Therefore, they would like 
Department to take precautionary steps so that States timely contribute their share and 
the Schemes are implemented flawlessly.  The Committee would also like the Department 
to ensure that the proposal under submission is approved at the earliest so that the 
proposal is implemented from 2026-27 onwards. 
8.25 The Committee appreciate the efforts of the Department and the initiatives taken 
by it for the welfare of Senior Citizens over the years. In order to have better management 
the Department has proposed to associate State/UT Governments in the implementation 
of the Schemes.  The Committee also feel that the available machinery with the senior 
citizens Division of the Department is not sufficient to cater to the requirement of the 
senior citizens. The Department has also received suggestions from various quarters for 
a separate dedicated Department for the welfare of senior citizens. The Department 
should examine the infrastructure available in the Department to manage the affairs of 
Senior Citizens. As is already known that the population of Senior Citizens in the country 
is projected to increase from 8.4% to 14.9% of the total population by 2036, and a small 
Division in the Department cannot be expected to cater to the increasing population of 
senior citizens. The Committee would also like to draw the attention towards the creation 
of separate Department for Divyangjan in 2012 by the Government. The separate 
Department was created to manage the affairs of comparatively less population of 
Divyangjan in the country and is effectively catering to their needs. The Committee would 
also like to express that once the ‘Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior 
Citizens (Amendment) Bill, 2019 is enacted the responsibilities of the Division will 
multiply. In view of the large population of Senior Citizens which continues to increase 
every year, the Committee would like the Government to examine creation of a separate 

89  
dedicated Department under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment as has 
been created for Divyangjan to ensure greater focus on policy matters relating to Senior 
Citizens and better coordination among stakeholders.

NATIONAL ACTION FOR MECHANIZED SANITATION ECOSYSTEM (NAMASTE) 
 
NAMASTE, a joint initiative of the MoSJE and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs 
(MoHUA), is being implemented since FY 2023-24. The scheme envisages safety and dignity of 
sanitation workers by creating an enabling ecosystem that recognizes sanitation workers as one 
of the key contributors in operations and maintenance of sanitation infrastructure thereby 
enhancing their occupational safety through capacity building and improved access to safety 
gear and machines. Components of erstwhile Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of 
Manual Scavengers (SRMS) have been subsumed in NAMASTE scheme from 2023-24. Further, 
waste pickers have been added as target group under NAMASTE in FY 2024-25. The Key 
Interventions of the scheme are as follows:- 
 
A. Sewer and Septic tank Workers (SSWs) 
Interventions  
(i) Profiling of Sewer/ Septic Tank workers. 
(ii) Distribution of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits to identified 
SSWs 
(iii) Distribution of safety devices to ERSUs 
(iv) Imparting occupational safety training to SSWs 
(v) Health insurance coverage of SSWs and manual scavengers and their 
dependents under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (after profiling of SSWs by 
ULBs) 
(vi) Upfront capital subsidy upto ₹7.50 Lakh for individual projects costing upto 
₹ 15.00 lakh for sanitation related projects and capital subsidy of ₹25.00 
Lakh for a group project of five sanitation workers including manual 
scavengers for a project costing ₹ 50.00 Lakh. 
(vii)Appointment of Responsible Sanitation Authority (RSA) in every District. 
(viii)Constitution of Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) in larger 
Urban Local Bodies (ULB) of Districts to cover Urban and Rural areas.  
(ix) Operationalization of Helpline number (14420). 
(x) IEC Campaign: Targeting Safai Mitras, Operators/ Contractors and 
Citizensthrough RWAs etc. through print and digital media, innovative 
media interventions and by organizing workshops/webinars 
  

91  
B.  Waste pickers  
Waste Pickers have been included as an additional target group along with sewer 
septic tank workers under NAMASTE scheme. The identified waste pickers would 
later on be provided occupational/ up gradation training for waste value addition. The 
scheme has various components for welfare of waste pickers namely profiling, Health 
Insurance under AB-PMJAY, Social Security Benefits, Occupational Safety Training, 
PPE Kits, Capital Subsidy for Dry Waste Collection Centres (DWCCs) to procure 
Waste Collection Vehicles and other welfare measures. The waste pickers 
component of the Scheme intends to integrate waste pickers in the solid waste 
management by addressing challenges, difficulties faced by them by mainstreaming 
them in the society, recognizing and strengthening their contribution in waste 
collection, recovery & recycling, providing safe, dignified and sustainable livelihood 
by empowering them through various interventions. Department of Social Justice & 
Empowerment, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, National Health Authority, 
National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation, Ayushman 
Bharat Empanelled Hospitals and Waste Pickers are the major stakeholders. The 
core objective of the Scheme is to ensure that waste pickers live dignified lives and 
work in a safe environment by enabling their enumeration, recognition and integration 
into the solid waste management value chain, while ensuring access to social security 
and welfare schemes based on their occupational identity.
