Report
The tourism has been a major social phenomenon of the societies all along.  It is motivated by the natural urge of every
 human being for new experience, adventure, education and entertainment.  Tourism is a multi sectoral activity characterized by
 multiple services provided by a range of suppliers.  It is largest service industry in the country.  Its importance lies in being an
 instrument for economic development and employment generation.   The tourism has been pivotal in social progress as well as
 an important vehicle of widening socio-economic and cultural contacts throughout human history.  A wide array of interests-
entertainment, sports, religion, culture,  adventure, education, health and business- drives tourism through increased contact.   It
 helps to promote cultural cohesion and social bonding and creates a durable social fabric.  With the advancement of transport,
 communication and improvement in general economic well being the demand for tourism has increased manifold.   The Five-
Year Plan perspective initiatives required for the development of tourism synergize with the development efforts needed to
 accomplish a number of other goals like employment generation, advancement of women and disadvantaged groups.  The
 Government plays a crucial role in making provision for tourism infrastructure and skill development. Such initiatives
 catalyses private enterprises to come forward and invest in this sector.  The share of India in international tourist arrival
 continues to increase from 2004 onwards.  But the share is still low at 0.55% in 2007.  The foreign tourist arrival rose from
 3.46 million in 2004 to an estimated 5 million in 2007.  Further more, foreign exchange earnings from tourism in India rose
 substantially from US$3 billion in 2002 to an estimated US$ 11.96 billion in 2007.  The share of India in world’s tourism
 receipts scaled from 0.65 per cent in 2002 to 1.21 percent in 2006. 
2.         The Ministry of Tourism is the nodal agency for the formulation of national policies and programmes and for the
 coordination of activities of various Central Government agencies, State Governments/Union Territories and the Private Sector
 for the development and promotion of tourism in the country.  The Ministry of Tourism plays a crucial role in coordinating and
 supplementing the efforts of the State/Union Territories Governments, catalyzing private investment, strengthening
 promotional and marketing efforts and in providing trained manpower resources. The function of the Ministry of Tourism
 mainly consists of the following:-
·
        Framing of policy matters on development of tourism
·        Grant of Central Financial Assistance to States/UTs for Development of Tourism Infrastructure
·        Encouragement of Public Private participation in tourism infrastructure development
·        Promotion and marketing of Tourism Products within the country and abroad
·        Providing incentives in the accommodation sector
·        Regulation of tourism industry
·        Investment facilitation
·        Human Resource Development and Training
·        Research, analysis, monitoring and evaluation
·        International Cooperation of promotion and development of India Tourism
3.         The administrative head of the Ministry is the Secretary (Tourism).  The Secretary also acts as the Director General
 (DG) Tourism. The office of the Director General of Tourism {now merged with the office of Secretary (Tourism)} provides
 executive directions for the implementation of various policies and programmes.  Directorate General of Tourism has a field
 formation of 20 offices within the country and 13 offices abroad and one sub-ordinate office/project i.e. Indian Institute  of
 Skiing and Mountaineering (IISM)/Gulmarg Winter Sports Project (GWSP). The activities of IISM/GWSP have been revived
 and various ski and other courses are conducted in the J&K valley.  In addition to the Headquarters Organization at New Delhi,
 the Directorate General of Tourism has 20 India Tourism Offices including 5 Regional Offices, situated at New Delhi,
 Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata , Guwahati and other offices are located at Agra, Bhubaneswar, Aurangabad, Bangalore, Kochi,
 Hyderabad, Imphal, Jaipur, Khajuraho, Naharlagun, Panaji (Goa), Patna, Port Blair, Shillong and Varanasi.  There are 13 India
 Tourism Offices Overseas, which include 5 Regional Offices at, New York, Frankfurt, Dubai, Sydney and Tokyo.  The other
 India tourism Offices are located at Los Angeles, Toronto, London, Paris, Amsterdam, Milan, Johannesburg and Singapore.
 The overseas offices are primarily responsible for tourism promotion and marketing in their respective areas and the field
 offices in the country are responsible for providing information service to tourists and to monitor the progress of field projects. 
 4.        The Ministry of Tourism has the following public sector undertaking and autonomous institutions under its
 administrative control namely :
            (i)        India Tourism Development Corporation  Ltd.(ITDC);
(ii)       Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management    (IITTM);

up from the present level to meet the investment targets.   The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of

22.       The Committee notes that one of the reasons for underutilization of allocation is unspent balances with the States and
 also non-submission of utilization certificates by most of the States on time.  The Committee observes that most of the time the
 Central Government delay release of funds to the State or releases it at the fag end of the financial year and expects the States
 to utilize it in a very short time.  The Committee criticize this practice as obviously the States are not in a position to spend the
 entire amount in such a short period and therefore, have unspent balance lying with them.   The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that the release of the funds to the States should be made on time so that they could utilize the amount rationally
 under proper monitoring of expenditure.   The Committee also desires that there should be proper coordination with the States
 Government, so as to obtain utilization certificates and to safeguard that money released is spent only on approved
 infrastructure development projects.
23.       The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is making efforts to develop quality tourism infrastructure at major
 tourist destinations and circuits for developing tourist products and providing better services to both domestic and international
 tourists.  The Committee observes that tourism is one of the economic sectors in the country that has the potential to grow at
 high rate and can ensure consequential development of the infrastructure of the destinations and circuits.  The Committee feels
 that the infrastructure development holds the key to India’s sustained of growth in the tourism sector,  therefore, tourist sites
 and destinations needs to be carefully selected on the basis of their potential to provide all infrastructural  facilities  required by
 the tourists within such destinations and circuits.   The Committee is of the opinion that, if, India has to exploit its vast inherent
 potential  in tourism, then it must provide exclusive quality tourism product and destinations comparable with other Asian
 countries like Singapore, Malaysia, Maldives, Thailand and China. As tourism cannot develop independent of other
 infrastructure, therefore, a lot of information dissemination is required in addition to hospitality and the scope and reach of the
 domestic tourism should also be broadened through development of these competitive destinations and circuits.   The
 Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to develop quality tourism at identified tourist circuits and destinations with
 focus on mega destinations and circuits that match international standards and satisfy the domestic and international tourists.  
 The aggressive marketing and publicity of these destinations and circuits should also be done to generate a niche market for
 Indian tourism products.   The Committee also urges the Ministry that while selecting a destination or a circuit they should
 attach priority for harmonious growth and development of all the Regions and States. 
24.       The Committee also recommends that in order to maximize the impact of investment on tourism infrastructure, the
 Ministry should make efforts for convergence of these mega destinations and circuits and projects with Jawahar Lal Nehru
 National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) for integrated development of infrastructure services, urban renewal, asset
 management and urban governance.

 regime through introduction of ‘Visa-on- Arrival’.  The justification for implementation of the ‘Visa-on- Arrival’ scheme is as
 follows:
(i)         The Department related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport Tourism & Culture on Demand for grants
 (2007 – 08) of the Ministry of Tourism, in its  119th  report  had recommended for  ‘Visa-on- Arrival’ scheme.
(ii)        Large number of foreign tourists plans their tours at the last moment, and as such, it becomes difficult for them to
 adopt the normal procedure of obtaining visa.  Therefore, the choice for selecting the destination is limited, and
 they select the destination, where the facility of ‘Visa-on- Arrival’ is available.
 (iii)      The Indian Embassies, High Commissions and Consulates are situated invariably in the capital cities of the
 countries except in a few countries, where additional Consulates are also located. Consequently the tourists have to
 travel from the far flung areas to the Indian Missions for obtaining visa.  This procedure involves extra time and
 expenditure for the foreign tourists.
89.       The Ministry of Tourism has been taking up the issue of ‘Visa on Arrival’ for quite some time:
(i)         The issue of ‘Visa-on-Arrival’ was discussed by the Group of Ministers in January, 2005 in which it was agreed
 in principle to introduce the scheme of ‘Visa-on- Arrival’ for sixteen identified countries.
(ii)        Further the matter was discussed in the Committee of Secretaries Meeting in  May, 2005 in which Secretary
 Tourism impressed upon the issue of “Visa on Arrival”. However, representative of, Intelligence Bureau was
 apprehensive that taking advantage of the scheme, undesirable elements may get entry in the country, but he
 was asked to examine the proposal in detail.
(iii)       Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs in September, 2006 expressed reservation for granting ‘Visa on Arrival’
 for security reasons. However, the Home Ministry in November, 2006 informed that ‘Long Term Tourist Visa’
 for five years duration with multiple entry facility has been approved for eighteen countries, which mainly
 consisted of sixteen countries recommended by GoM for ‘Visa on Arrival’. This long term visa carries
 stipulation of 90 days on each visit (Annexure-III).
(iv)       In the meeting of Empowered Sub-Committee of the Committee on Infrastructure held in January 2007, it was
 agreed that Foreign Secretary could deliberate with the Home Secretary to sort out the bottlenecks in the
 implementation of ‘Visa-on- Arrival’ for tourist from sixteen identified countries at Delhi and Mumbai Airport. 
 In continuation of this, the Ministry of External Affairs in January 2007 had requested the Home Ministry for
 implementation of ‘Visa on Arrival’ scheme for foreign tourist from sixteen select countries.
(v)        The Ministry of Home Affairs had informed that during the inter ministerial consultation held in August, 2007
 the issue of ‘Visa on arrival’ was discussed at length and in this meeting the security agency expressed the
 views that on account of prevailing global security scenario and the present infrastructural constraints at
 International Airport, it may be desirable to defer the introduction of the ‘Visa on Arrival’ Scheme for some
 time.
(vi)       The Home Ministry has reiterated the same stand through their letter dated November 26, 2007.

            The Committee observes that the Ministry of Tourism projected a requirement of Rs.5405.58 crore  (10% basis)
 and Rs. 6569.61 crore (20% basis) for the entire 11
th Plan against this requirement, the Planning Commission approved
 an allocation of Rs.5156.00 crore  for carrying out major activities of the Ministry viz. Augmentation of Tourist
 infrastructure, Development of Human Resource for hospitality and travel trade, Promotion and Publicity, Creating
 budget accommodation etc.  The Committee also notes that in the Annual Plan 2008-09 the Ministry has projected an
 outlay of Rs.1062.85 crore  against which an amount of  Rs.1000.00 crore was allocated.  The Committee deplores the
 tendency of Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance for imposing cuts on the amounts demanded by the
 Ministry.  This mismatch between projected amount and sanctioned outlay may result in widening further the gap
 between the tourism potential and development of tourism synergies for achieving the goals.   The Committee feels that
 in order to attain the National growth targets in the 11
th Plan Period, huge planned funding is required.  Thus, the

th Plan

 caution and remedial action to absorb in time the allocation made to them.

            The Committee notes that during 2007-2008, the plan outlay of Rs. 996.62 crore  of Ministry of Tourism was not
 subjected to any cut at RE stage.  However, the Committee notes that during the year 2007-08, out of the budgeted
 allocation of Rs. 996.62 crore , the Ministry  could spent Rs. 658.55 crore upto December, 2007 which clearly indicates
 the poor fiscal management in the Ministry  of Tourism. The Committee observes that the major portion of the

(Para 87)
            The Committee is perturbed to note that lack of connectivity is the major impediment for the growth of tourism
 in India.  The Committee feels that there exists a large domestic tourist movement in the country but in the absence of
 poor access to the places of tourist interest, the tourist cannot be encouraged to visit such places.   The Committee is of
 the view that domestic tourism cannot be promoted unless air, rail and road links across the country and especially the
 places of tourist interest are improved to desired level.   The Committee recommends that tourist destinations in the
 country should be well connected with the rail, road and air to ensure the easy accessibility to these places.  In order to
 improve the connectivity to tourist sites, the Ministry of Tourism should have done coordination with Ministry of
 Railways and Civil Aviation for promotion of tourism in the country.  The Ministry of Railways should provide better
 quality of rail services to encourage tourists to travel by train.  The basic amenities like drinking water, toilets, tea-
coffee, parking facilities and well-maintained clean waiting rooms and potters with trolleys   should also provided at the
 railways stations connecting these mega destination.   The Ministry of Civil Aviation should develop infrastructure
 facilities at Airports to meet the rising air traffic requirements and quality of service at the airports connecting mega
 destinations.  The domestic and foreign carriers should also be encouraged to increase air seat capacity from overseas
 markets.  The helicopter services for remote areas, like Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and North-eastern
 region  may also be initiated by the Ministry of Civil Aviation as a measure to promote tourism in a big way.

MULTIPLICITY OF TAXES
            The Committee is constrained to notes that luxury tax on hotel, VAT on food and beverages and on Airlines

 at large.  The Ministry of Tourism has forwarded two proposals for consideration of  Empowered Committee of State
 Finance Ministers and Department of Road Transport and Highways respectively, in this regard and a decision is
 awaited.  The Committee strongly criticizes the lackadaisical approach of the Government in the matter which have
 adversely affected the growth of tourism and hospitality sector in the country.   The Committee reiterates that the
 Government must provide a level playing field to the tourism and hospitality sector including tourist transport by
 attempting to rationalize taxes or eliminate the disparity in tax treatment as levied by the different States and Union
 Territories.  The Committee recommends the Ministry to pursue vigorously the matter of rationalization of taxes with

 recommends the Government to set up an Empowered Group for rationalization of roads and transport taxes on
 tourist vehicles.  
(Para 91)
VISA-ON-ARRIVAL SCHEME
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has taken up the matter of the issue of visa on arrival facility
 on pilot basis  to tourists with the Ministry of External Affairs and Ministry of Home Affairs for 18 select countries. 
 The Committee welcomes that the Ministry of Home Affairs has taken a decision to grant long term tourist visas 5 years
 duration with Multi - entry facilities to the nationals of the 18 countries and introduction of Advanced Passenger
 Information System (APIS).  However, the step is not sufficient to achieve the objective.  The Committee feels that with
 the liberlisation of visa regime and introduction of multiple entry long term tourist visa for tourist and implementation
 of APIS would facilitate tourist arrival in the country and will increase India’s share in global tourism markets.  The
 Committee recommends the Ministry to purse the matter with the Ministry of Home Affairs for expediting introduction
 of multiple entry long term tourist visa, provide visa on arrival facilities on pilot basis to the nationals of 18 countries
 and implementation of APIS.  The Committee also cautions the Ministry that in no way the security considerations of
 the country be compromised. 
(Para 97)
SPECIAL TOURISM POLICE
            The Committee is constrained to note that incidents of cheating, fleecing, criminal acts and harassment of foreign
 tourists including gender abuse mar the image of the country and have an adverse impact on the foreign tourists
 arrival. The Committee feels that the issue related with safety and security is paramount and needs to be looked into
 seriously.  The Committee is aware the linkages between Centre and States in the federal set-up and appreciates the
 efforts of the Ministry in persuading the States for creation of tourist police force for ensuring the safety and security of
 the tourists.   The Committee also notes that the Ministry of Tourism is formulating guidelines regarding formation of
 tourist police force and has taken several steps to curb the menace of cheating, over charging and victimization of
 tourists.  The Committee feels that in the critical situation, the role of media, travel agents and tour operators is crucial
 in establishing goodwill and image of that country. The Committee recommends the Ministry to take initiatives for
 deployment of special Tourist Police in the reamining States and bring out a guide lines on the formation of tourism
 police so as to address the safety and security related issues in a big way.    The Committee also desires that the police
 personnel of the States should also be provided special tourist oriented training.

            The Committee notes that the tourism is multi-disciplinary activity and cannot be developed at its own. The

 Urban Development, Civil Aviation, Shipping and Road Transport and Highways, Home, Finance etc. The Committee,

REPORT
India is one of the few nations in the world having a developed culture and a fast
developing economy. Its culture is deeply rooted in a pluralistic society. Development of culture
should be considered as a catalyst to the economic development. As such culture cannot be
confined to the boundaries of any particular sector. However, it could be recognized that there
are certain sectors wherein presence and contribution of culture and creativity are much more
dominant and visible. Elements of culture encompass media, films, music, handicrafts, visual arts,
Performing Arts, literature, heritage management, cultural and creative industries etc. The Cultural
development inter-alia  includes areas of Culture both in tangible and intangible fields.
2. The mandate of the Ministry of Culture is to preserve and promote all forms of art and
culture. To this end, the Ministry of Culture undertakes the following activities :
• The maintenance and conservation of the country’s heritage, ancient monuments and
historic sites;
• Promotion of the literary, visual and performing arts;
• Administration of libraries, museums and anthropological institutions;
• Maintenance, preservation and conservation of archival records and archival libraries;
• Research and development in the conservation of cultural property;
• Observation of centenaries and anniversaries of important national personalities and
events;
• Promotion of institutions and organizations of Buddhist and Tibetan studies;
• Promotion of institutional and individual initiatives in the field of art and culture;
• Entering into and implementation of cultural agreements with foreign countries;
3. The functional spectrum of the Ministry ranges from generating cultural awareness at the
grassroots level, to promoting cultural exchanges at an international level. Along with programmes
for the preservation of India’s ancient heritage, the activities of the Ministry encourage and
disseminate a variety of contemporary creative arts as well. The Ministry’s aim is to develop
ways and means through which the basic cultural and aesthetic sensibilities of the people remain
active and dynamic. The activities are carried out through the two attached offices, i.e. ,
Archaeological Survey of India and National Archives of India; seven subordinate offices and
thirty-three autonomous institutions working under the Ministry.
The following are the subordinate offices under the Ministry of Culture:
• Anthropological Survey of India, Kolkata
• National Museum, New Delhi
• National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi
• National Library, Kolkata

2
• Central Reference Library, Kolkata
• National Research Laboratory for Conservation of Cultural Property, Lucknow
BUDGET ALLOCATION AND OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF THE FINANCIAL
PERFORMANCE FOR THE YEAR 2007-08
4. Demand No. 18 containing the details of the budget allocation of the Ministry of Culture
for the financial year 2008-09 was considered by the Department-related Parliamentary Standing
Committee on Transport Tourism and Culture at its meeting held on the 26th March, 2008. For
the year 2008-09, the Ministry of Culture has been allocated Rs. 1025.00 crore including the plan
component of Rs. 600.00 crore.
5. The Ministry informed the Committee that as against Rs. 4965.99 crore proposed by the
Ministry, for Art and Culture Sector for the Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12), the Planning
Commission has tentatively allocated Rs. 4024.00 crore. Thus, keeping in view the allocation in
2007-08 and 2008-09, the allocations for the next three years will have to increase substantially
for Ministry of Culture.
6. The Ministry further stated that they had projected demand of an Plan Outlay of
Rs. 864.73 crore for 2008-09 on the basis of the proposals received from various cultural
organizations, divisions under the Ministry. The Planning Commission has allocated a sum of
Rs. 600.00 crore for developmental activities thereby resulting a cut of Rs. 264.73 crore for the
year 2008-09 on account of resource constraints. This cut has an effect on almost all the
sectors of the Ministry including organizations such as Archaeological Survey of India,
Akademies, Zonal Culture Centres, National Council of Science Museums, Science Cities,
departmental central schemes and the new schemes of the Ministry of Culture.
7. The sector-wise break up of plan and non-plan allocation for the year 2008-09 is as
follows:

8. The Committee notes that the expenditure trend during 2007-08 is not very
satisfactory. For the plan allocation, expenditure of Rs. 370.39 crore has been incurred out
of the RE of Rs. 520.00 crore. In the non-plan also, expenditure of Rs. 298.00 crore has
been incurred out of Rs. 460.00 crore upto 29th February, 2008. Thus, Rs. 149.61 crore
in plan and Rs. 161.28 crore in non-plan remained to be utilized in the month of
March, 2008.
9. Regarding low utilization of funds, while considering the A TNs, the Committee was
informed by the Secretary that the Ministry has a very large number of small and diverse
activities which is probably causing the underutilization of funds. During the RE exercise in the
month of November by the Finance Ministry, the BE of Ministry of Culture has been reduced
invariably. The Secretary, Ministry of Culture has expressed its constraints:

3
‘‘One is that, about a quarter of our expenditure is done by the ASI which is not a
CPWD type but nevertheless of a work related expenditure which can only happen after
the monsoon and, therefore, gets into the second half of the year... Secondly, cultural
activities do come in, in an odd way because of cultural season which is really winter
and thereafter. Therefore, we have this second half of the year type of expenditure.
Usually the Ministry is able to spend 53% by December, however, the Ministry of Finance
desires that only 33 per cent of the allocation can be spent in last quarter. Thus, the
Ministry of Culture finds itself at a disadvantage.’’
10. The Committee in its 120th Report, had recommended to the Ministry of Culture that the
review of budgetary allocation by Government in the month of December may be taken up
instead of the month of September of the financial year. Subsequently, this matter was taken up
with the Ministry of Finance for their views/comments. In this regard, the Ministry of Finance
have shown their inability to alter the reviewing system of budgetary allocation, since the
preparation of budget documents for presentation of Annual Budget on 28th February starts from
December and it is, therefore, necessary to complete their R.E. exercise before this, which is
done during October-November every year.
11. The Ministry of Culture informed the Committee that the reduction in the budgetary
provision at RE stage from the original provision for the Ministry every year affects important
ongoing activities as well as proposed activities included in the Plan allocation made to cultural
organizations of the Ministry of Culture. This reduction in the budgetary provision hampers the
growth of cultural organizations especially development of infrastructural facilities including
building component, application of modern techniques and IT related techniques in their
functioning. Therefore, it is felt that the cultural organizations including autonomous organizations
need to be funded adequately to meet their developmental activities.
12. The Committee is unhappy to note that despite its concern and considered
recommendation, the Ministry of Finance has refused to review the budgetary allocations
in the month of December instead of in the month of September thereby subjecting the
Ministry of Culture to financial cuts at RE stage. The Committee observes that there is
a greater need and scope for scrutiny of entire exercise of Budgetary Process beginning
from budgetary proposals in September by the Ministry of Finance in respect of Ministry
of Culture because of its special needs. The Committee feel that the entire budgetary
process and procedure involving about eight months has actually given both to the evil of
mis-utilisation of funds in a hurried manner and apprehension of losing valuable but
scarce financial resources made available to them by Ministry of Finance at the fag end
of the financial year. It appears that given the rigidity in budgetary exercise the Ministry
of Finance has failed to assess actual requirements of the Ministry of Culture for funds
to be utilized for various developmental purposes. The Committee is of the firm belief
that the underutilization to a great extent in the Ministry of Culture is the result of rigid
financial practices and procedures. The Committee therefore, recommends the Planning
Commission and Ministry of Finance for giving an active consideration through a rigorous
and rational scrutiny for reforming and rescheduling of the present Budgetary procedures
and practice as far the Ministry of Culture is concerned, so that the final plan and non-
plan allocations are conveyed to the Ministry and to respective Institutions/organizations
by the month of December every year for effective and fruitful utilization of scarce
financial resources. Alternatively, the Committee recommends that the possibility may be
explored for provision of budget allocations for various activities may be converted as non-
Iapsable fund taking into account the seasonal nature of work and activities undertaken
by various institutions under the Ministry of Culture.

4
13. The Committee is happy to note that for the first time, allocation for the Ministry
of Culture has reached to four figures. The Committee feels that it is a good beginning
for this vital sector which has huge potential but yet to be explored. The Committee
hopes that all the new schemes and projects taken up by the Ministry during the financial
year 2008-09 will be completed in a time bound manner.
14. The Committee also recommends that possibility of organising off-season festivals
and organizing Dance/Cultural programmes throughout the year may be explored. The
Ministry should also explore for decentralization of some of the schemes which can help
the Zonal Centres in expediating their work. This will certainly help in providing much
needed relief to the Ministry. The Committee also recommends that inspite of the
constraints faced by the Ministry, there is need to spread the expenditure evenly and
making efforts for full utilization of the allocated amount through proper planning and
monitoring. Only then the desired result for Eleventh Five Year Plan can be achieved.
15. The Secretary while deposing before the Committee informed that the Ministry of Culture
has set up three-member Committee of the Ministry to look at the performance of various
schemes, to try and improve them, make them perhaps even more flexible or decentralise them,
and improve their quality. They are trying to improve the capacity to spend properly in time.
16. The Committee notes the efforts made by the Ministry to improve its performance.
The Committee may be apprised of the findings of the three members Committee and the
steps proposed to be taken to improve the performance of various schemes being
implemented by the Ministry of Culture.
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA (ASI)
17. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) was established in 1861. It is an attached
office of the Ministry of Culture. The major activities undertaken by ASI are: maintenance,
conservation and preservation of centrally protected monuments/sites and remains. In addition to
the above activities, it conducts archaeological exploration and excavation and underwater
archaeology regularly. Since its inception, the ASI has grown into a large organization having its
network of 24 circles throughout the country. There are 3667 monuments of National importance
in the country which are Centrally Protected Monuments, which include 21 properties inscribed
on the World Heritage List by UNESCO. ASI is also engaged in developing epigraphically
research, setting up and reorganization of site museums, imparting training programmes in
Archaeology, strengthening of the Chemistry Branch and Horticulture Branch. Publication
programme of ASI encompassing the fields such as academic, informative and awareness
generation is one of the important activities of ASI. This programme will be strengthened further
during the year 2008-09 so that more publications relating to archaeology could be brought out
for the general public, particularly for students.
18. In the BE 2008-09 the ASI has been provided with Rs. 312 crore consisting of plan
component of Rs. 111.00 crore. While emphasizing the importance of ASI, the Ministry of
Culture has informed the Committee that the increase in the budgetary allocation will benefit
mainly the Archaeological Survey of India and the building projects of National Gallery of
Modern Arts. The Committee drew attention of the Ministry of Culture to the problem vanishing
of centrally protected monuments. In the reply, the Secretary, Ministry of Culture during the
course of evidence submitted to the Committee:
‘‘... regarding the monuments which appear to be vanishing and which do not seem to
find trace. There are about 30-odd such monuments which we ourselves are now trying

5
to see where exactly and when they went out of the book. But, Sir, it is not easy
because some of these are not available for quite some time. It is not a recent
phenomenon per se . Some of them, I am given to understand by my Archaeologist
colleagues, are, actually, available. They know where it is but, maybe, it is covered by
water. They know that it is there but it is not protected in that sense. Since there is a
need to go into all these in detail, we have set up recently an internal committee within
the ASI to study this and come back with the factual position and, perhaps,
recommendations in this area. It has been recently done. That is something we would be
looking at.’’
19. The Committee notes that the cases of vanishing of our monuments is a dangerous
process which if not controlled in time, may lead to a situation where we will be left with
only a few monuments as symbols of our culture and tradition. The vanishing of
monuments should be stopped with all the resources at our disposal. The Committee notes
that the Ministry has already taken appropriate measures to prevent it. The Committee
may be apprised about the findings of the internal Committee to study the problems and
the steps taken to implement the findings with the result it achieved.
20. The Committee notes that the allocation for ASI has been reduced from BE 2007-08 of
Rs. 98.00 crore to Rs. 89.00 crore at RE stage. The main reason for reduction of allocation
at RE 2007-08 was that Rs. 10.00 crore under Sub-head 03 00 50 (other charges) was
earmarked in the BE 2007-08 for the National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities. Since the
NMMA is yet to be fully operationalized and State level implementation committees are not yet
formed, projects to be approved by them are yet to take off. Consequently, the allocation for
NMMA had to be reduced drastically at RE stage. Other sectors in which provision was
substantially reduced (in percentage terms) at RE Stage are Archaeological Site Museums and
externally aided programme. This work is now in advanced stages and the projects will take off
during 2008-09. In externally aided projects (JBIC project at Ajanta-Ellora) the low expenditure
level is due to time taken in completion of certain formalities. The increased allocation of

35. Set up as an Imperial Records Department in 1891 in Calcutta, this Department was

informed that during the period between 2005 and 2007, no case has been registered by them
relating to smuggling of antiquities. There are number of smuggling cases reported before this

awareness among people and to identify, nurture and promote the vanishing folk art traditions in
the rural and semi urban areas of the States. The objectives of these centers are to provide local
creative support to folk and traditional artisans. They are:—
(a) Promotion of various art forms especially the folk art of the Zone.
(b) Setting up of Shilp Grams in each Zonal Cultural Centre to provide promotion and
marketing facilities to craftsman.
(c) National Cultural Exchanges Programme, exchange of artists, musicologists,
performers and scholars from one region to another within the country.
(d) Development of Infrastructural Facilities.
69. Two more activities have been entrusted to the Zonal Cultural Centres from the year 1993
viz. Republic Day Folk Dance Festival and Craft Fair; and Documentation of vanishing Folk Art
Forms. The zonal cultural centres will continue its major ongoing schemes during 2008-09 which
inter alia  includes national cultural exchange programme, documentation and publication, national
folk dance festival, shilpgram , guru-shishya parampara , theater rejuvenation, scheme for
recognition to young talented artists, crafts fare on republic day, Kurukshetra Utsav, training of
street children and slum area children and north-east festival. Plan allocation for Zonal Cultural

16
Centres in BE 2007-08 was kept at Rs. 13.00 crore. However, at RE stage Rs. 11.00 crore has
been allocated and expenditure upto February, 2008 is Rs. 10.88 crore.
70. The Committee is of the view that protection and promotion of vanishing folk art
tradition. is a very important mandate and in order to implement the mandate Zonal
Cultural Centre should enroll artists associated with different folk art tradition and
provide them adequate remuneration. For this purpose the amount allocated for the year
2008-09 may be fully utilized and if possible allocation may be enhanced next year for the
purpose. The Committee also recommends that the Zonal Cultural Centres should expand
their activity to include the use of culture as an effective tool of national integration.
SETTING UP OF MULTI PURPOSE CULTURAL COMPLEXES INCLUDING THOSE FOR
CHILDREN
71. Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided to an autonomous body created by
State Governments to set up art complexes. The objectives of the schemes are that the quality
of life of young people be made sensitive to what is aesthetically and morally good in our
society. This can be done by exposing them to the finest forms of creative expression from an
early age. Cultural complexes for children will provide these avenues for our young people.
Multipurpose cultural complexes of general nature foster and coordinate activities in the State in
the different cultural fields such as music, drama, dance, literature, fine arts etc. and promote
through them the cultural unity of the country. Under the present terms and conditions, there
will be two categories of MPCC.
Category I:  It will be an integrated complex consisting of auditorium, with green rooms and
toilets, library/documentation centers, museum, exhibition gallery, storage space, conference hall/
seminar room, guest room/dormitory, children’s activity corner, cafeteria etc. (It is only an
indicative list of facilities). The project cost shall be limited to Rs. 5.00 crore and only one
MPCC will be allowed in each State under this category.
Category II: It will be a smaller version which may include any or all of the facilities like
auditorium, library/reading hall, workshop facilities etc. The project cost of this category shall be
limited to Rs. 2.00 crores and there can be more than one such MPCC in a State.
72. From the year 2007-08, the scheme of Multi Purpose Cultural Complexes was
discontinued at the instance of Planning Commission. It was desired that by the Planning
Commission that the MPCC Scheme may be restructured as a central sector scheme. For the
Tenth Five Year Plan, tentative allocation of Rs.80.00 crore has been made and in RE 2007-08
Rs.3.60 crore has been provided and expenditure incurred is Rs. 2.25 crore. For 2008-09,
allocation of Rs. 2.00 crore has been made.
73. The Committee notes that ceiling of the project cost fixed for single cultural
complex of Category-I is Rs. 5.00 crore and for Category-II smaller version cultural
complex is Rs. 2.00 crore. Whereas, the total allocation made for MPCC in the BE
2008-09 is only Rs. 2.00 crore. The Committee is at a loss to understand the rationality
behind this less allocations as even for a Category II MPCC an amount of Rs. 2.00 crore
is required. The Committee feels that this kind of approach will promote only adhocism.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the modalities for running the scheme may
be worked out and the scheme may be widely publicized for utilization of allocated
resources. The Committee may be apprised about the details of the number of MPCCs
already established till the last financial year and the details of the proposed MPCCs. The
Committee would also like to know the benefits of converting it into a Central Sector
Scheme.

KALAKSHETRA FOUNDATION, CHENNAI
74. Kalakshetra has become the center of excellence especially in the field of dance, drama
and music. The Foundation aims to arrange for training, research, study, teaching and
development of art and science, music, dance, drama, fine arts and Bharat Natyam. Recognising
the importance of the institution, the Government of India took over the management of
Kalakshetra on 29 September, 1993 and declared it as an Institution of National importance. The
Foundation has the constituent units such as, College of Fine Arts; Craft Education and Research
Centre consisting of a weaving department and Kalamkari Unit; Besant Arundale Senior Secondary
School; Besant Theosophical High School; and Besant Cultural Centre Hostel.
75. The plan allocation in BE 2007-08 of Rs.2.50 crore was reduced at RE level to Rs.2.05
crore. Further allocation has been enhanced at BE 2008-09 to Rs.3.00 crore to strengthen and
widen the activities of Kalashetra. The expenditure reported upto 29th February, 2008 is Rs.1.26
crore which shows underutilization of funds in 2007-08.
76. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should monitor the utilization of
funds more closely for Kalashetra and help the organization in planning/executing the
allocated fund judiciously and evenly throughout the year. The Committee observes that
with the increased budgetary allocation the Kalakshetra Foundation and its constituent
units will be able to strengthen their activities. The details of fund utilizations for each
of the activity may please be furnished to the Committee.
NATIONAL MISSION FOR MANUSCRIPT
77. The National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM) is the first consolidated national effort for
reclaiming India's inheritance of knowledge contained in the vast treasure of manuscripts.
Manuscripts, which contained centuries of accrued knowledge in such areas as philosophy,
sciences, literature, arts and the pluralistic faith systems of India are more than just historical
records. They represent the collective wisdom and experience of generations of thinkers. The
Mission was established in 2003 with the objective of creating a national resource base for
manuscripts, scattered across the country. The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts is the
nodal Agency for its implementation.
78. The Ministry informed the Committee that major achievement of the Mission since its
inception are total electronic data of manuscripts and total data stock and collection of 25,000
repositories from various institutions and private collections. The National Survey of Manuscript
has surveyed 16 States in total and survey preparation is underway in the States of Madhya
Pradesh, Sikkim Arunachal Pradesh, Pondicherry, Goa, Jammu and Kashmir (Laddakh) Uttrakand,
U.P., Bihar, and Jharkhand. Post survey documentation has been conducted only in 8 States,
namely Orissa, Bihar; Manipur, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh Tamil Nadu, Keral and Himachal
Pradesh.
79. The plan allocation in BE 2007-08 was Rs. 8.50 crore which was reduced to
Rs. 6.37 crore at RE stage. The allocation was stepped upto Rs. 9.00 crore in BE 2008-09. The
Mission was able to utilize the entire allocation of RE by 29th February, 2008.
80. The Committee notes that the pace of the Mission is very slow. The Committee
recommends that the Mission should augment its target to conduct post survey
documentation in all the States. The survey and documentation process should be
completed in a time-bound schedule. The Committee further recommends that the
exhibition of Indian Manuscript at various premier National and International fora should
also be given thrust and the mission should initiate proactive measures in this regard.

ACADEMIES AND NATIONAL SCHOOL OF DRAMA
SAHITYA AKADEMI
85. Sahitya Akademi was set up on 12 March, 1954 by the Government of India as an
autonomous organization fully financed by the Government. The Sahitya Akademi is the premier
institution in the country for literary dialogue, literary publication and promotion. It is the only
institution in the country that undertakes publishing and promotion of literature in 24 Indian
languages including English and to promote through them the cultural unity of the country.
Sahitya Akademi proposes to undertake activities like purchase of books in 24 languages,
publishing around 300 books in all the 24 languages, providing travel grant to about 40 young
writers and to organize/participate in about 100 books exhibitions at National/regional/international
level during 2008-09.
86. Plan allocation for Sahitya Akademi of Rs. 9.75 crore was marginally reduced at RE
level to Rs. 9.60 crore and further enhanced to Rs. 10.50 crore in BE 2008-09. The increased
outlay is for of fice building of Akademi.
87. The Committee recommends that steps may be taken to popularize the activities of
Sahitya Akademi among the population and particularly the students of Universities and
premier institutions throughout India. At present its existence is known only to the
literary circles. More emphasis may be given to national integration and secularism
through literature. It has also a role to popularize our democratic values and rids cultural
heritage.
SANGEET NATAK AKADEMI
88. The Sangeet Natak Akademi is a national institution for promotion of performing arts. The
Akademi has three constituent units namely (i) Kathak Kendra, New Delhi (ii) Jawaharlal Nehru
Manipur Dance Academy, Imphal and (iii) Rabindra Rangshala, New Delhi. The Akademi is
devoted to the furtherance of the performing arts in India, and seeks to achieve this by arranging
performance by renowned artists as well as by young talented artists through training
programmes, awards of scholarships, documentation, etc. The Akademi has National Institutes
and centers for specialized fields such as Kutiyattam Centre at Kerala and Chhau Centre at
Baripada/Jamshedpur.

scheme of organizing Music, Dance and Theatre festivals, seminars, work shops on music,
dance and theatre. Plan allocation in BE and RE 2007-08 was Rs. 10.50 crore. The expenditure
reported upto 29th February, 2008 is Rs. 12.36 crore.
90. The Committee notes that Sangeet Natak Akademi has been able to spend more
than the allocated amount. The Committee r ecommends that the Sangeet Natak Akademi
should endeavour to establish national institutes and centres for each of our dance forms
and performing arts, it need in association with the State Governments.
91. The Committee was informed that the Sangeet Natak Akademi has approached the Lt.
Governor of Delhi for allocation of 5 acres of land for the proposed National Museum for

within 2-3 years.

Development Authority in a time bound manner and if need be the issue may be taken
up at Ministerial level. The Committee recommends to the DDA that they should speed
up the process of land allotment to the Sangeet Natak Akademi at the earliest. The
Committee may be apprised about any procedural or administrative delay in the allotment
of land and construction of the building.
LALIT KALA AKADEMI
93. Lalit Kala Akademi (the National Academy of Arts) was established in 1954 for promotion
of visual and plastic arts in India like Painting, Graphic, Sculpture, Ceramic, etc. The Akademi
organizes Regional, National and International exhibitions regularly and also participates in various
Biennial and Triennial being organized by other countries abroad. In the past 50 years of its
existence, the Akademi has provided invaluable contribution to the Promotion of visual arts in
India by organizing exhibitions artists camps, Kala Melas and bringing out art publications.
94. The Committee notes that the plan allocation of Rs. 5.50 crore was reduced to

96. National School of Drama (NSD) is one of the foremost theatre training institutions in the
world and the only one of its kind in India. It was set up by Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1959
as one of its constituent units. In 1975, it became an independent entity and since then it is
functioning as an autonomous organization under Ministry of Culture. Since its inception, the
School has not only made great strides in the area of theatre training but has also diversified
its activities. Besides the training programme, which is of 3 years duration, the School has
explored new vistas in the areas of Children Theatre and decentralization of theatre training
through organizing workshops.
97. The Plan allocation of Rs. l1.00 crore in BE 2007-08 was enhanced at RE stage to
Rs. 13.50 crore and expenditure reported upto 29th February, 2008 is Rs. 14.00 crore. During
the year 2008-09, National School of Drama proposes to expand its activities in North East

Region by augmenting the scheme of National Theatre Festival and North East Region Theatre
Development. NSD proposes to organize Theatre workshops, to assist 15 theatre groups and to
organize part time courses during 2008-09, NSD will organize its Golden Jubilee Celebrations
during 2008-09. NSD also proposes to open 5 Drama Schools in different regions during
2008-09.
98. The Committee is pleased to note that National School of Drama is planning to
undertake lot of activities in the year 2008-2009. The Committee hopes that National
School of Drama will be able to fulfill its commitment in 2008-09 by planning its activities
in phased manner.
NEHRU MEMORIAL MUSEUM AND LIBRARY (NMML)
99. The Nehru Memorial Museum and Library was established in 1966 as a memorial to
Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of Independent India. Besides maintaining a
personalia museum focussing on the life and times of Jawaharlal Nehru, the major objectives of
this autonomous institution which is under the Ministry of Culture are to acquire, maintain and
preserve the personal papers and other historical material pertaining to nationalist leaders and
institutions of Modern India; to establish and maintain an advanced library on the history of
Modern India in all its aspects and to promote research in the fields of Modern Indian History
and Society. The Nehru Memorial Museum and Library (NMML) all through these years has been
successfully pursuing the aims and objectives set out in its Memorandum of Association and in
the process has continued to sustain and improve upon a tradition of excellence and commitment
to historical scholarship.
100. Plan Allocation for Nehru Memorial Museum and Library in BE and RE 2007-08 was
Rs. 3.50 crore. Additional provision of Rs.20.00 crore was provided for development and
modernization of NMML in accordance with the Finance Minister’s Budget Speech. Expenditure
of Rs. 22.45 crore was made upto 29.2.2008. Allocation in BE 2008-09 is Rs. 4.00 crore.
101. The Director, Nehru Memorial Museum and Library informed the Committee that—
‘‘The main focus of this proposal, and half the money, Rs. 20 crores, is allocated for
a massive digitisation programme for the archival resources of the Nehru Memorial
Museum and Library. We have about Rs. 90 lakhs of archival documents. We have about
1000 collections of what are called private papers, beginning from Nehru to lot of
business papers, to Salim Ali and Mohammed Bashir. It is really now the largest non-
official archives in India. And this is really frontier work and it has not even happened
in many parts of the world. We plan to digitise this entire collection, put it on Internet
and hopefully, if there are no legal and other difficulties about certain papers, put it right
on to the Net and make it searchable down to the last word. That is the kind of
technological up gradation that we have been working on. So, I have been working with
people at various levels, technological and others, to put together this whole project. We
have done pilot studies and done the research. We have really put together what we
know. This would cost us about Rs. 3 crores and 50 lakhs to digitise about 35 lakh
documents in the first stage. Then, coming to newspapers, we have about 110 lakh pages
of newspapers in all Indian languages. Beginning with English and Hindi, we would like
to digitise 20 lakhs of pages out of these 110 lakhs and that would take us another
Rs. 5 crore. To set up the digital archival management system, the hardware, etc. it
would cost another one crore rupees and the personnel, etc. would cost us about half
a crore of rupees. So, we have a Rs. 10 crore budget for this. We will try to do most
of this over the next year, beginning now, but some of it may necessarily spill over. The
second part of this is the modernisation of the existing library and we have allocated
Rs. 2 crore for that.’’

the selection process for award of fellowships in Nehru Memorial Museum and Library. In
response to the points raised by the Committee, the Secretary, submitted that
‘‘We have looked at that case. We find there was a gap. I must admit that I am saying
this from memory at the moment. There was a period where the new committee was set
up and there was an accusation made that the NMML didn't follow procedures. But, Sir,
to my understanding, as an academic organization, they follow the norms of other
academic institutions. They are granting fellowships. They don’t go only by the
application method. It is a bit of a search committee approach and that has been there
in the past. It is not for the first time that this has happened. I believe that universities
like JNU also follow this approach. So, there has been no deviation in that sense from
the rules or systems of the organization.’’
103. The Committee appreciates the initiatives taken by the Nehru Memorial Museum.
and Library for modernization and digitization. The Committee however, recommends that
the award of fellowships by the NMML must be transparent and beyond any criticism as
the fellows who apply for the fellowships are eminent scholars who never compromise any
type of nepotism or favouritism or procedural irregularities.
SCIENCE CITIES
104. Science Cities, at selected centres in the country were proposed to be set up during the
Ninth Five Year Plan. The Science Cities will be comprised of a Science Exhibition Hall, the
mass Science Area and a Science Park, The location of Science City should be either the State
Capital or one important city of the State having a sizeable population. Moreover, the state
Governments may provide the infrastructure facilities to these Centres free of cost. The total
cost of setting up of a Science City may be between Rs. 65-70 crores. The State Governments
and Societies/authorities promoting the setting up of Science Cities are eligible for financial
assistance from the Central Government under its Plan funds.
105. W ith the available funds during 2008-09, it is also proposed to set up Science Cities at
Ahmedabad, Allahabad, Hyderabad and Mangalore. Funds are also allocated for Regional Science
Centres at Raipur, Ranchi, Dharwad, Mangalore, Coimbatore, Jaipur and Science City, Bangalore
and sub-regional centres at Solapur and Kalimpong.
106. Plan allocation of Science Cities in BE 2007-08 was 13.00 crore which was reduced to
Rs. 10.89 crore at RE stage. The expenditure incurred upto February, 2008 was Rs. 7.89 crore.
Allocation in BE 2008-09 is Rs. 12.00 crore.
107. The Committee recommends that adequate plan outlay should be provided in the
Budget to ensure that science cities are set up in all the state capitals of the country and
while fixing priority every year parity should be drawn amongst the regions.
SPREADING INDIAN CULTURE ABROAD
108. Cultural Agreements and Cultural Exchange Programmes are concluded with various
countries, with a view to projecting India’s culture and promoting bilateral cooperation between
India and other countries in the field of art and culture, education and sciences, films mass
media, public health, sports agriculture etc. by way of exchange of scholars, exhibitions and
sport, teams, exchange of books and publications, exchange of Radio and T.V . Programmes,

award of scholarships and development of Institutions abroad through Indian Council for Cultural
Relations. Government of India have cultural agreements with 115 countries, out of which
specific biennial and triennial cultural exchange programmes have been entered into with 82
countries. For this purpose non plan allocation of Rs. 80 lakhs has been made.
109. The Ministry of Culture continued to provide funds towards meeting the annual
contributions to International Centre for Conservation, Rome (Rs.10.00 Lakh), World Heritage
Fund (Rs.7.00 lakh) and Contribution to UNESCO (Rs. 14.00 Lakh). The Ministry has been
given with Rs. 31.00 lakh as non-plan allocation for contribution to international bodies in BE
2008-09. The Festival of India abroad and reciprocal festivals of other countries in India was
started in 1982 with the objective of projecting India’s rich cultural heritage and contemporary
creativity abroad. The Festival of India has so far been held in UK, USA, Japan, Sweden,
Germany, China, Thailand and Bhutan. The Festivals of France, USSR, Japan, Sweden, China and
Germany were held in India on reciprocal basis. During the year 2008-09, it is proposed to
organize ‘‘India Week’’ in Brazil. It is also proposed to organize Festival of India in United
Kingdom during 2008-09. For conducting festivals of India Rs. 4.l0 crore has been granted to
the Ministry as non-plan budget in the BE 2008-09.
110. The Committee appreciates the efforts in spreading Indian culture abroad by
holding seminars, fairs and festivals. The Committee recommends that the festivals
should be highly focused and highlights every region of the country so as to promote
tourism and culture of all the States. The Committee also recommends that some
countries should be selected where these festivals should be held continuously for some
years so as to make an impact on the population there.

114. The Ministry of Culture informed that an 18 member Committee has been constituted to
look into the framing of a National Culture Policy. The Committee held two meetings so far, the

Culture Policy by April, 2008.
HERITAGE SITES COMMISSION BILL
116. The Committee was informed that the Government is considering to set up a Heritage
Sites Commission as part of measure for protection and conservation of cultural and natural
heritage. A Bill for the purpose is under preparation in consultation with the concerned Ministries/
Departments. The requirement of funds for functioning of the Commission would be known after

overdue measure.
NATIONAL CULTURE FUND
118. The National Culture Fund (NCF) was set up in November, 1996 as a trust under
Charitable Endowment Act, 1890 with the aim of inviting the participation of the corporate
sector, NGOs, State Governments, Public/Private Sectors and individuals in the task of
promoting, protecting and preserving India’s cultural heritage as well as creation of new galleries,
museums and imparting of training in cultural activities. The donations to the National Culture
fund are eligible for 100 per cent tax exemption under Section 10 23C (iv) and 80 G (ii) of
the Income Tax Act. The NCF is managed and administered by a Council and an Executive
Committee. NCF is required to propagate its objectives in a big way through advertisements and
massive public relation efforts to mobilise sufficient funds.
119. At the time of constitution of NCF, it was decided that a corpus of Rs. 19.25 crore
would be provided by Ministry of Culture.

26
120. The Committee notes that the plan allocation of Rs. 3.00 crore was the same at RE
stage and further step-up to Rs. 3.19 crore in BE 2008-09. The expenditure reported upto
29th February, 2008 is Rs. 3.00 crore. The Committee was informed that as on
31st March, 2007 the position of funds is as under:
(i) Corpus of the NCF Rs.19,67,85,853/-
(ii) Donations/ Contributions from Corporates and
other Organisations Rs.16,24,60,639/-
(iii) In addition Rs. 26 crores were received from Indian Oil Corporation which was
immediately transferred to Indian Oil Foundation for adoption of One Monument
in each State.
121. The Committee suggests that the PSUs and Private Industries which are directly or
indirectly using the monuments and sites of culture for their commercial motives have an
obligation to contribute to the National Culture Fund. The Committee recommends that
the Ministry should identify and enumerate those PSUs and Private Industries which are
using the Monuments and Cultural Sites and may be cajoled to contribute to the NCF.
The Committee further recommends that more PSUs/Organisations Corporate Houses
should be approached to donate for NCF. The Committee also recommends that the
utilization details of the NCF may be submitted to it.
NORTH EAST REGION
122. The States in the North Eastern Region are often considered to be at disadvantageous
position owing to their geographical isolation and poor infrastructure. The Ministry has been
taking many initiatives to highlight and popularize the rich and diverse art and culture of the
North Eastern States, including Sikkim. Various activities would be organized in North Eastern
States during the year 2008-09 through North East Zonal Cultural Centre at Dimapur and
Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Akademi at Imphal. In addition to their activities, the Ministry
and its attached/subordinate offices and autonomous organizations propose to undertake activities
in North East Region by extending their spectrum of activities to the North Eastern Region. In
order to implement the scheme effectively and utilize the funds allocated under North East to the
optimum level, many organizations have endeavoured to tie up their activities with local partner
organizations, like having tie up with NEHU by Sahitya Akademi and with local Akademies by
other National Akademies. Efforts are also being made by other organizations to tie up with their
respective local partners for improving their performance in North East.
123. An amount of Rs.60.00 crore has been allocated by the Ministry for various activities
during 2008-09. This amount has been allocated under various Divisions in respect of schemes
directly operated by them and the organizations (Attached/Subordinate Offices and Autonomous
Organizations) for taking up activities in North East during 2008-09, as proposed by them. The
Ministry of Culture also provides grants to Tawang Monastery, Arunachal Pradesh; Namgyal
Institute of Tibetology, Gangtok, Sikkim; and Buddhist Cultural Preservation Society, Arunachal
Pradesh. During 2007-08, adequate funds for development of Tawang monastery was provided.
During 2008-09, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (CIHTS), V aranasi has come up with
a proposal of an activity relating to development of medicinal plants in North Eastern Region.
A provision of Rs.30.00 lakhs has already been kept for this purpose under North East for
CIHTS. Last but not least, an institute called Central Institute of Himalayan Culture Studies at
Dahung in West Kameng District, in the State of Arunachal Pradesh is proposed to set up by
the Ministry of Culture. This institute is presently running courses for the Purva Madhyama

27
and Uttar Madhyama. The Institute is proposed to be established as an autonomous body. One
of the major objectives of the Institution would be to prepare students for higher learning and
research in the field of Buddhology, Bhoti language and literature and Himalayan studies with
adequate knowledge of modem research methodology and advanced techniques and to inculcate
awareness for ecological balance and preservation of natural resources. The budgetary provision
towards this institute would be for its overall development inclusive of adequate infrastructural
facility. A sum of Rs. 5.00 crore has, therefore, been kept during 2008-09 under North East for
funding this Institute.
124. On the recommendation of the Parliamentary Standing Committee under Para 61 of
120th Report many autonomous organizations under the Ministry of Culture have tied up with
local partners like Universities, NGOs, State Akademis and State Government Departments in
order to implement their programmes effectively and to utilize the allocated funds for the North
East Region including Sikkim.
125. The Ministry informed that archaeologically speaking, the North Eastern States of India
are largely unexplored, and sites still lesser excavated, chiefly owing to non presence of a
dedicated field office for the purpose. Although, there is an ASI Circle Office in Guwahati, but
it is largely engaged in activities like preservation and conservation of archaeological monuments.
It being tough hilly terrain, and further difficult to access because of high rainfall zone, the
exploration and excavation objectives of the region defined by Assam and six sister states of the
east remain unrealized. The multitude of diverse ethnic tribes of these states are a major source
for anthropological and ethnographic studies to contribute to wide-ranging understanding of
human cultures and past societies of this region. Hence, there is ample scope for the rich
archaeological studies through a new Excavation Branch, with its headquarters at Guwahati. The
proposal of creating an Excavation Branch for the North-East States was also proposed in the
Tenth Five Year Plan document, but somehow this aspect remained unrealised.
126. Plan allocation for North Eastern region in BE 2007-08 of Rs. 55.70 crore was reduced
at RE stage to Rs. 47.00 crore. The allocation has been substantially increased in BE 2008-09
to Rs. 60.00 crore.
127. The Committee is anguished to note that despite its earlier recommendations,
Rs. 20.00 crore of the allocation remained unspent for the North-East Region. This shows
the neglected attitude towards the North Eastern region where even the reduced RE
allocation remained unutilized. The Ministry should make concerted efforts to utilize the
funds by proper implementation of schemes so that the North Eastern region which is still
unexplored gets its due share.
128. The Committee notes that the Excavation of Branch for the North East States
remains unrealized in the 10th Five Y ear Plan. The Committee recommends that the
Excavation Branch may be included as one of the items in the Eleventh Five Year Plan
and implemented within the presumed time frame. If required this matter may be taken
up at the highest level to sort out the issues involved in establishing the Excavation
Branch in the North East.
129. The Committee notes that lot of initiatives had been taken with huge fund
allocation by the Ministry to implement various activities in the North East. It is not
clear what are the benefits accrued to the North East due to such enhanced allocations
and whether the allocated money is really spent for the purposes it was allocated. The
Committee therefore recommends that a study or an inquiry may be conducted to see
what are the actual benefits of the enhanced allocation and whether the fund allocated

28
are utilized for the purposes for which these were allocated. The feed back of the study
may be furnished to the Committee.

stage.

OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
BUDGET ALLOCATION AND OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF THE FINANCIAL
PERFORMANCE FOR THE YEAR 2007-08
The Committee notes that the expenditure trend during 2007-08 is not very
satisfactory. For the plan allocation, expenditure of Rs. 370.39 crore has been incurred out
of the RE of Rs. 520.00 crore. In the non-plan also, expenditure of Rs. 298.00 crore has
been incurred out of Rs.460.00 crore upto 29th February, 2008. Thus, Rs. 149.61 crore
in plan and Rs. 161.28 crore in non-plan remained to be utilized in the month of
March, 2008. (Para 8)
The Committee is unhappy to note that despite its concern and considered
recommendation, the Ministry of Finance has refused to review the budgetary allocations
in the month of December instead of in the month of September thereby subjecting the
Ministry of Culture to financial cuts at RE stage. The Committee observes that there is
a greater need and scope for scrutiny of entire exercise of Budgetary Process beginning
from budgetary proposals in September by the Ministry of Finance in respect of Ministry
of Culture because of its special needs. The Committee feel that the entire budgetary
process and procedure involving about eight months has actually given both to the evil of
mis-utilisation of funds in a hurried manner and apprehension of losing valuable but
scarce financial resources made available to them by Ministry of Finance at the fag end
of the financial year. It appears that given the rigidity in budgetary exercise the Ministry
of Finance has failed to assess actual requirements of the Ministry of Culture for funds
to be utilized for various developmental purposes. The Committee is of the firm belief
that the underutilization to a great extent in the Ministry of Culture is the result of rigid
financial practices and procedures. The Committee therefore, recommends the Planning
Commission and Ministry of Finance for giving an active consideration through a rigorous
and rational scrutiny for reforming and rescheduling of the present Budgetary procedures
and practice as far the Ministry of Culture is concerned, so that the final plan and non-
plan allocations are conveyed to the Ministry and to respective Institutions/organizations
by the month of December every year for effective and fruitful utilization of scarce
financial resources. Alternatively, the Committee recommends that the possibility may be
explored for provision of budget allocations for various activities may be converted as non-
lapsable fund taking into account the seasonal nature of work and activities undertaken
by various institutions under the Ministry of Culture. (Para 12)
The Committee is happy to note that for the first time, allocation for the Ministry
of Culture has reached to four figures. The Committee feels that it is a good beginning
for this vital sector which has huge potential but yet to be explored. The Committee
hopes that all the new schemes and projects taken up by the Ministry during the financial
year 2008-09 will be completed in a time bound manner. (Para 13)
The Committee also recommends that possibility of organising off-season festivals
and organizing Dance/Cultural programmes throughout the year may be explored. The
Ministry should also explore for decentralization of some of the schemes which can help
the Zonal Centres in expediting their work. This will certainly help in providing much
needed relief to the Ministry. The Committee also recommends that in spite of the
29

30
constraints faced by the Ministry, there is need to spread the expenditure evenly and
making efforts for full utilization of the allocated amount through proper planning and
monitoring. Only then the desired result for Eleventh Five Year Plan can be achieved.
(Para 14)
The Committee notes the efforts made by the Ministry to improve its performance.
The Committee may be apprised of the findings of the three members Committee and the
steps proposed to be taken to improve the performance of various schemes being
implemented by the Ministry of Culture. (Para 16)
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA (ASI)
The Committee notes that the cases of vanishing of our monuments is a dangerous
process which if not controlled in time, may lead to a situation where we will be left with
only a few monuments as symbols of our culture and tradition. The vanishing of
monuments should be stopped with all the resources at our disposal. The Committee notes
that the Ministry has already taken appropriate measures to prevent it. The Committee
may be apprised about the findings of the internal Committee to study the problems and
the steps taken to implement the findings with the result it achieved. (Para 19)
The Committee hopes that ASI will learn from its past experience on the reasons
for underutilizations of allocated funds and take appropriate steps to utilize the allocated
resources. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take immediate steps to
operationalise NMMA and expedite formation of State level implementation Committees
so that funds are utilized within the financial year. The Committee may be apprised
about the steps taken to operationalise NMMA and the status of its implementation.
(Para 21)
The Committee notes that more than 56 excavation reports are pending with ASI
since 2002. The Committee is of the views that this is a serious matter since there is
inordinate delay in the preparation of reports. The Committee hopes with the new system
in place, there will be no delay in preparation of reports on excavation in future.
(Para 24)
The Committee notes the steps taken by the Ministry to prevent encroachments.
The Committee desires that possibility of making financial provision to pay for the
rehabilitation of the encroachers who are removed from monuments may also be explored
in consultation with Ministry of Finance so that the Ministry is not dependent on
respective State Government for rehabilitation of encroachers. (Para 26)
The Committee also notes that more than 249 centrally protected monuments have
been encroached upon by various elements due to multifarious reasons. Some of the
reasons are historical whereas some others are socio-economic in nature. The Committee
observes that the problem needs to be addressed on a permanent basis with a lasting
solution wherever possible. Appropriate mechanisms may be evolved to rehabilitate the
encroachers and the Government should ensure the retrieved monuments are not illegally
occupied again. The Committee notes that an appropriate Committee may be constituted
to look into the various aspects of the encroachments with the mandate to recommend
appropriate mechanism for finding a solution. This may be done on a time bound basis.
(Para 27)
The Committee recommends that to preserve the national heritage from
defacement, penal punishment under the Act should be suitably revised to deter the

31
culprits along with other positive steps like generating awareness towards protection and
maintenance of beauty of the Monuments as valuable national heritage. (Para 29)
The Committee notes that the advertisements in the print and electronic media to
create awareness among the population about bad effects of defacement of monuments is
giving an impetus to the tourism sector. The Committee feels, the propaganda mechanism
needs to be more strengthened by introducing appropriate curriculum in the school
syllabus on the bad effects of defacement of our monuments. Moreover, the Committee
notes that a special campaign may be launched to educate the school children for the
preservation of our monuments. In addition to this, the media campaigns should also
focus the legal punishments involved in defacement of our national heritages. (Para 30)
The Committee appreciates the efforts of ASI for putting India on the world map
by undertaking conservation work in Cambodia and hopes that similar projects may be
taken up in other countries also. (Para 32)
ANTHROPOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
